DS-A11Y-001.rule: Every interactive element has a hit area of at least var(--hit-area-min) in both dimensions. The visual element can be smaller. Extend the hit area with a pseudo-element, and never size the visible control with this token. On a coarse pointer (any-pointer: coarse) the minimum is var(--hit-area-coarse) (48).

DS-A11Y-002.rule: `:focus-visible` — triggers only when the browser determines a visible focus indicator is needed. This covers keyboard navigation and assistive technology, but not mouse clicks. Use this for focus rings on buttons and links

DS-A11Y-005.rule: `<button>` for actions. `<a>` for navigation. Not `<div onClick>`.

DS-A11Y-006.rule: Form inputs need associated `<label>` elements, not just placeholder text.

DS-A11Y-011.rule: Use `<ul>` or `<ol>` for lists of items. Don't use a stack of `<div>` siblings when the content is semantically a list.

DS-A11Y-019.rule: Every dialog has an accessible name (DialogTitle or AlertDialogTitle, visually hidden if the design shows none). An AlertDialog also has a description that says what will happen.

DS-A11Y-020.rule: First focus in a dialog: the close button in a destructive dialog that has one, otherwise Cancel (never the destructive button), the first field in a form dialog, the primary action in a confirmation that is not destructive.

DS-A11Y-021.rule: When a dialog closes, focus returns to the element that opened it. If that element is gone, focus goes to the nearest sensible place, never to the top of the page.

DS-A11Y-022.rule: Escape closes a dialog, and a click on the scrim closes a Dialog (not an AlertDialog: Radix blocks that on purpose). Block Escape and the scrim only while closing would lose money, a delete or a legal step in progress, and keep a visible Cancel when you do.

DS-A11Y-023.rule: Anything the user can do by dragging can also be done with a single tap or the arrow keys (WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.5.7, Dragging Movements).

DS-A11Y-030.rule: A Select, Combobox or Command input has an accessible name from its visible label (`<label htmlFor>` or `aria-labelledby`). Use `aria-label` only when the design shows no label. The chosen value shown in the trigger is not a name.

DS-A11Y-032.rule: Every tab has a text name (`aria-label` when the tab is an icon). When a page has more than one tab list, each tab list has its own `aria-label`.

DS-A11Y-034.rule: A toast is announced in a polite live region (assertive only for an error that needs attention now), keeps showing while it is hovered or has focus, and stays long enough to read. A toast never holds the only copy of a result or the only way to do an action: the page shows the same result.

DS-A11Y-035.rule: A Switch, Checkbox or Radio has a visible text label that is tied to the control (a wrapping `<label>` or `htmlFor`), so a click on the label toggles it. A Switch label names the setting ("Email alerts"), not the action, and does not change when the state changes.

DS-A11Y-036.rule: A menu or popover closes on Escape and returns focus to its trigger, as a dialog does (DS-A11Y-021, DS-A11Y-022). Build them from Radix (`DropdownMenu`, `Popover`), not from a positioned `div`.

DS-A11Y-037.rule: A Spinner or Skeleton that stands for loading has a text name ("Loading orders") in a polite live region, or `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading. A spinner with no text next to it is not decoration.

DS-ANIMATION-004.rule: Always respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Users who set this have real reasons — vestibular disorders, epilepsy, motion sensitivity.

DS-COLOR-003.rule: Color cannot be the only signal. Error states, success states, warnings — always pair color with an icon, label, or text. Never rely on color alone.

DS-COLOR-008.rule: Status color comes from four semantic roles: `info`, `positive`, `negative`, `notice`. Each role has a token in the Base layer and in every System layer, named after the Figma variables: `--base-{role}`, `--bg-{role}`, `--text-{role}`, `--border-{role}`, `--icon-{role}`. Components that show status (Alert, Badge, Toast, inline validation, banners) use these tokens. Never a palette class or a literal color for status, and never a one-off token invented for it.

DS-COLOR-009.rule: Pick the status role by meaning, not by hue. `info` is neutral context. `positive` is success or completion. `negative` is an error, a failure, or a destructive action. `notice` is caution or something that needs attention before it becomes an error. There is no separate `destructive` token: a destructive Button reads `--base-negative`, and `destructive` is only the shadcn variant name. Older names (`--color-destructive`, `--color-success`, `--color-warning`, `--color-{role}-surface`) become the Figma tokens: `warning` is `notice`, a surface is `--bg-{role}`.

DS-COMPONENT-001.rule: Check the manifest first. If `<Button>`, `<AlertBanner>`, or `<DataTable>` exists, use it. Don't rebuild it.

DS-COMPONENT-007.rule: Control heights come from the size tokens. Button heights are 28 (`--size-action-medium`), 36 (`--size-action-large`) and 48 (`--size-action-x-large`), and 36 is the default on web, 48 on native. The circular action is 56 (`--size-action-circular`) and no other action or control is 56 (an avatar can be, and so can the `icon-lg` icon button on a coarse pointer, DS-ICON-003). Input and Select are `--size-field-web` (36) on web and `--size-field-native` (48) on native. `--size-field-compact` (32) is only for an inline field nested in a table or a dense row. A Button next to a field matches the field's height.

DS-ELEVATION-002.rule: Use the five elevation tiers from Figma, `--shadow-base` to `--shadow-xlarge`, and match each element to the tier in `data/elevation-map.json`. Card, Choice Card and the segmented indicator rest at Base. Card hover, resting Choice Card hover, Switch knob and Hover Card are Small. Menus and select lists are Medium and pair with the dropdown z-index. Dialog and Tooltip are Large and pair with the overlay or modal z-index. XLarge is only for a dragged item or a full-screen surface. Layers run in role order (page, dropdown, overlay, modal), so don't put a heavier shadow on a lower layer than on the one above it. The exception is a popup opened from a dialog (menu, select, hover card, tooltip): it stacks above the modal and keeps its own lighter tier.

DS-ELEVATION-005.rule: In dark mode, never use a shadow alone. Base and Small carry no shadow: a lighter fill step than the parent and a 1px hairline border carry them. Medium and up use a blacker shadow plus the hairline. A 4 to 5% black shadow is invisible on a dark surface. The tokens exist: `--elevation-surface-small`, `--elevation-surface-raised` and `--elevation-surface-popup` (a menu, select list or hover card, one step above a Dialog) for the fills, `--elevation-hairline` for an edge (transparent in light), and `.dark` redefines `--shadow-base` to `--shadow-xlarge`, so a component that reads a tier token gets the dark shadow for free. Set the fill and the edge yourself from the surface and hairline tokens. Do not hand-write dark values.

DS-ELEVATION-006.rule: A panel docked to an edge casts its shadow away from that edge, not on all sides. Right-docked: negative x. Left-docked: positive x. Bottom-docked: negative y. Top-docked: positive y. Centered: x is 0. Use a negative spread so the shadow does not leak past the panel. Use the directional token for the side: `--shadow-large-right`, `-left`, `-bottom` or `-top` (Large only today), and record the side in the map's `dock` field.

DS-GLASS-001.rule: Frosted glass is opt-in and goes only on chrome and floating layers: a sticky nav bar, tab bar or toolbar; a menu, popover or dropdown; a dialog, sheet or command palette; an icon button floating over an image, video or map (Button variant="glass"). Never on the content layer (body text, a data table, a form, a card in a list). At most 3 glass surfaces in one viewport.

DS-ICON-002.rule: If an icon's surrounding text size doesn't map cleanly to one of the four defined sizes (16/20/24/32px), round to the nearest one rather than introducing an arbitrary size. The Button sets one more on its own, a 28px glyph for `icon-lg` on a coarse pointer (DS-ICON-003); never set 28 by hand.

DS-ICON-003.rule: Icon-button sizes follow the Button heights: `icon-sm` 28 with a 16 glyph, `icon` 36 with a 20 glyph (the default), `icon-lg` 48 with a 24 glyph. On a coarse pointer (`@media (any-pointer: coarse)`, not the screen width) they step up to 36/20, 48/24 and 56/28. The target is at least 44 (48 on a coarse pointer) through invisible expansion (DS-A11Y-001). Never smaller than `icon-sm`, except a button inside a field and a chip's remove control (DS-ICON-006). One icon-button size and one glyph size per row.

DS-ICON-005.rule: An icon-only button has an accessible name that says what it does (`aria-label="Add to favorites"`, not "Heart"), from `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or `sr-only` text. A Tooltip with the same text shows on hover and focus and never replaces the name. Use icon-only buttons only for actions everyone knows (search, close, add, delete, more, favorite, play).

DS-LAYOUT-WIDTH-001.rule: Form containers use max-width: var(--width-form-max). No hardcoded width values.

DS-MODAL-001.rule: Trap focus using `inert`. When a modal opens, add `inert` to all content outside the modal. This blocks keyboard and screen reader access to background content without manual focus trapping

DS-MODAL-002.rule: Prevent scroll bleed. Add `overscroll-behavior: contain` to the modal's scrollable container so scrolling inside doesn't scroll the page behind it

DS-MODAL-003.rule: Prevent layout shift. When a modal opens and the page scrollbar disappears, the layout jumps. Fix it with `scrollbar-gutter` on `html`

DS-MODAL-004.rule: The body of a dialog scrolls. The header and the footer stay in view. A tall dialog never scrolls its title or actions away.

DS-MODAL-005.rule: A dialog footer has a primary action and a secondary action (Cancel), both right-aligned. Typically that is all. A third action is a ghost or link button on the left, and only when the dialog is wider than 400px.

DS-MODAL-006.rule: Never nest modals. A second step replaces the content of the same dialog (push a view with a Back control) or becomes a page. A destructive confirmation from inside a dialog or sheet replaces its content the same way.

DS-MODAL-007.rule: Never use a modal for navigation. A list of places to go is a menu or a page.

DS-MOTION-001.rule: Timing and easing come from motion tokens (`var(--motion-duration-*)`, `var(--motion-ease-*)`, or `motion-tokens.ts` for Motion). Component code holds no literal durations, `cubic-bezier(...)` curves, or numeric easing arrays. Only the token file (`motion-tokens.{css,scss,ts,js}`) may define them.

DS-MOTION-002.rule: The slow duration token is for large elements only (drawers, sheets, modals entering). It can run up to 500ms. Any other UI animation stays under 300ms, whichever token it uses.

DS-MOTION-007.rule: Delight never gates the task and never carries meaning alone. A loop pauses under `prefers-reduced-motion` and while the page is hidden, nothing flashes more than three times a second, and a one-off occasion effect plays once and can be skipped.

DS-PANEL-001.rule: Use a push panel (inline, moves the main content) when people need to see the page and the panel together. Use an overlay panel (floats over the page) for a task that ends.

DS-PANEL-002.rule: Below --breakpoint-md every panel is full screen. No push, no half-width overlay.

DS-PANEL-003.rule: From --breakpoint-md a panel pushes only if window width minus --nav-rail minus the panel width leaves at least --main-min. Otherwise it is an overlay.

DS-PANEL-004.rule: While a push panel is open, the app shell keeps the full sidebar only if window width minus --nav-sidebar minus the panel width leaves at least --main-min. Otherwise the sidebar shows as the rail until the panel closes. Do this before turning the panel into an overlay.

DS-PANEL-005.rule: A push panel is --panel-push-default wide. If people can resize it, keep it between --panel-push-min and --panel-push-max. The main content never goes below --main-min.

DS-PANEL-006.rule: An overlay uses a size tier (--panel-overlay-sm, --panel-overlay-md or --panel-overlay-lg). Its width is the smallest of the tier and half the window width rounded down to a multiple of 4, and never under --panel-overlay-min.

DS-PANEL-007.rule: A list with a detail pane shows both side by side only if each pane gets at least --pane-min. Otherwise it behaves like a phone: the list alone, and the detail opens as its own screen with a back control.

DS-PANEL-008.rule: Panel and pane widths are token names. Never a raw number in code, in a template or in a design spec.

DS-RESPONSIVE-008.rule: Below --breakpoint-md a dialog that holds a choice (confirm, select, stepper, slider) is a bottom sheet: at most 90dvh tall, a stacked footer with the primary button on top, a visible Close or Cancel button, and dvh for its height.

DS-RESPONSIVE-010.rule: A bottom sheet and a full-screen form pad their edges with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), env(safe-area-inset-left) and env(safe-area-inset-right).

DS-SURFACE-004.rule: Buttons with text + icon: use less padding on the icon side, by the label inset. The label sits in a frame and the icon sits outside it. The label's inset is `--space-padding-2x-small` (4px) at the small size and `--space-padding-x-small` (8px) at default and large; the container padding is 8px at every size. So `icon-side padding = text-side padding - inset`, and the gap between icon and text is the inset. The Button's `leadingIcon` and `trailingIcon` already do this.

DS-TABLE-001.rule: A table has exactly one scroll owner, chosen on purpose. A sticky header sticks to its nearest scroll-container ancestor, and any overflow other than visible or clip creates one, so nothing between the header and the intended owner may change that by accident.

DS-TABLE-002.rule: A complex table's wrapper owns both axes: overflow: auto with a bounded block size, a sticky header inside it, scrollbar-gutter: stable, overscroll-behavior-x: contain, and scroll-padding-block-start equal to the header height.

DS-TABLE-003.rule: A simple table sets no overflow on its wrapper, so its sticky header sticks to the page (offset by any fixed app header), and it never scrolls sideways.

DS-TABLE-004.rule: Do not use overflow: auto clip, or overflow-x: auto with overflow-y: clip, to keep a header sticky to the page. clip computes to hidden next to auto, which is still a scroll container.

DS-TABLE-005.rule: Every flex or grid ancestor between the app shell and a table wrapper has min-inline-size: 0 and min-block-size: 0, so the table neither widens the page nor loses its bounded height.

DS-TABLE-006.rule: A pinned first column uses position: sticky with inset-inline-start: 0 and an opaque background. Layers are small local z-index values (pinned column 1, header row 2, corner cell 3) inside a stacking context made by isolation: isolate on the scroll owner, so they never outrank an overlay. Add scroll-padding-inline-start equal to the column width.

DS-TABLE-007.rule: Tables with sticky cells use border-collapse: separate with border-spacing: 0. Collapsed borders do not travel with sticky cells.

DS-TABLE-008.rule: Table layout changes key off the container, not the viewport: container-type: inline-size on an element outside the scroll wrapper, and @container (width < 37.5em) for the narrow layout.

DS-TABLE-009.rule: Use table-layout: fixed with explicit column widths, text-overflow: ellipsis on text cells, right-aligned numbers with tabular-nums, and left-aligned text.

DS-TABLE-010.rule: Style table scrollbars with scrollbar-width: thin and scrollbar-color from an existing neutral token such as the muted foreground. No ::-webkit-scrollbar. Do not hide the scrollbar on a table that scrolls sideways.

DS-TABLE-011.rule: scrollbar-gutter: stable on the scroll owner, so header and body columns stay aligned when a scrollbar appears.

DS-TABLE-012.rule: overscroll-behavior-x: contain on the scroll owner. Do not contain the vertical axis.

DS-TABLE-013.rule: scroll-padding-block-start equal to the sticky header height on the scroll owner, so focused rows are not hidden under it.

DS-TABLE-014.rule: A complex table that scrolls on both axes scrolls one axis per gesture: a wheel handler (passive: false, ctrlKey passes through) that scrolls only the dominant axis, shared as one hook, with an opt-out. Simple tables do not use it. Leave touch alone.

DS-TABLE-015.rule: A scroll owner has tabindex="0", role="region", and an aria-label. Keep real table elements, a button inside a sortable th, and aria-sort on the sorted th. Use role="grid" only with arrow-key cell navigation.

DS-TABLE-016.rule: Paginate by default. Virtualize only for database-style grids with thousands of rows, and test the sticky header and pinned column with a long scroll.

DS-TABLE-017.rule: Highlights for just-added or just-saved rows and any scroll-shadow transition respect prefers-reduced-motion.

DS-TABLE-018.rule: A table that scrolls sideways shows a cue that more content exists, such as an edge shadow on the pinned column or a partly visible column, because overlay scrollbars are hidden until scroll.

DS-TABLE-019.rule: Header height and row height per density come from the table_sizes tokens. Check the workspace token set first. If one is missing, propose adding it, never hardcode. The space above a complex table and a fixed app header's height are set by the page, not tokens, and the component supplies a fallback.

DS-TAILWIND-005.rule: Never `transition: all`. List properties explicitly: `transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, transform 150ms ease-out`.

DS-TOKEN-005.rule: With shadcn/ui, point each shadcn variable at its Vois token: `background` at `--bg-background`; `foreground`, `card-foreground`, `popover-foreground`, `secondary-foreground` and `accent-foreground` at `--text-primary`; `card` at `--bg-card`; `popover` at `--elevation-surface-popup`, so a stock shadcn popover, menu or select list is one step above a Dialog in dark and matches the Vois menus; `primary` at `--action-primary-resting`; `primary-foreground` at `--action-primary-text`; `secondary` at `--action-secondary-resting`; `muted` at `--bg-subtle`; `muted-foreground` at `--text-secondary`; `accent` at `--bg-hover`; `destructive` at `--base-negative`; `border` at `--border-pretty`; `input` at `--input-border`; `ring` at `--border-state-focus`; `radius` at `--radii-8`, so shadcn's derived steps land on the Vois radius roles (`md` 6, `lg` 8, `xl` 12).

PATH-A.name: Settings Page
PATH-A.condition: User is managing profile, workspace, team, billing, notifications, or members. Multiple related sections that don't need to be edited simultaneously. Changes persist immediately or on explicit save.
PATH-A.outcome: Use the Settings Page pattern. Depth (shallow vs. deep) is decided by PATH-A-DEPTH-SHALLOW / PATH-A-DEPTH-DEEP. Mobile: sidebar becomes a hamburger menu that slides out and overlaps content.

PATH-A-DEPTH-DEEP.outcome: Sidebar navigation + sub-pages. Structure: sidebar (pinned on desktop, hamburger on mobile) + main content area.

PATH-A-DEPTH-SHALLOW.outcome: Horizontal tabs pinned to top (single page). Structure: page title + tabs + tab content area.

PATH-B.name: Table/List with Details
PATH-B.condition: User needs to browse, search, filter, and act on multiple items. User occasionally dives into single item details. Bulk actions might be needed.
PATH-B.outcome: Use the Table/List with Details pattern. Decide simple or complex (PATH-B-SIMPLE, PATH-B-COMPLEX), then how a row opens (PATH-B-ROW-OPEN) and where editing happens (PATH-B-EDIT). Row detail: a drawer by default, with an Open action that escalates to a full page when the record has tabs, a timeline, related records, or a long form. Behavior inside the table is covered by the PATH-TABLE-* rules.

PATH-B-COMPLEX.name: Complex table
PATH-B-COMPLEX.condition: More than 6 columns, user-chosen columns or saved views, bulk actions, inline edit, many filter dimensions, or thousands of rows.
PATH-B-COMPLEX.outcome: Toolbar with search, filter builder, columns, density, and saved views. Checkbox column and bulk bar. The table wrapper owns scroll on both axes with a bounded height, header and first column pinned, scroll locked to one axis per gesture. Dense, Regular, and Comfortable densities.

PATH-B-EDIT.name: Where editing happens
PATH-B-EDIT.condition: A user edits data from a table.
PATH-B-EDIT.outcome: One atomic, low-risk value: inline cell edit. Several fields or cross-field validation: the drawer form. The same change on many rows: a bulk bar action or bulk edit page. Irreversible or high-impact: the drawer form plus a confirmation dialog.

PATH-B-NARROW.name: Table narrow layout
PATH-B-NARROW.condition: A table's container is narrower than the sm breakpoint value (37.5em).
PATH-B-NARROW.outcome: If the table has 4 or fewer columns, not counting the actions column, rows stack as list items. If it has more, the table scrolls horizontally with the first column and header row pinned.

PATH-B-ROW-ACTIONS.name: Row quick actions
PATH-B-ROW-ACTIONS.condition: A table or list row has quick actions.
PATH-B-ROW-ACTIONS.outcome: Two visible actions is preferred and three is the maximum. Everything beyond that, including secondary and destructive actions, goes in a DropdownMenu.

PATH-B-ROW-ACTIONS-REVEAL.name: Row actions on touch devices
PATH-B-ROW-ACTIONS-REVEAL.condition: A row's quick actions are revealed on hover.
PATH-B-ROW-ACTIONS-REVEAL.outcome: Reveal on hover only where the device supports hover. On touch devices the actions are always visible.

PATH-B-ROW-OPEN.name: Row open container
PATH-B-ROW-OPEN.condition: A user opens a row to see its record.
PATH-B-ROW-OPEN.outcome: Record has 8 or fewer fields and no related records: right-side drawer (the Sheet component in vois-components), view first with an Edit action or edit directly. From --breakpoint-md the drawer pushes the table aside when DS-PANEL-003 passes (the table stays usable beside it), and otherwise overlays it. Below --breakpoint-md it is full screen (DS-PANEL-002). Record has tabs, a timeline, related records, or a long form: full page, reached from an Open action in the drawer. Only a confirmation: Dialog. The open row id is in the URL and the active row stays highlighted.

PATH-B-SIMPLE.name: Simple table
PATH-B-SIMPLE.condition: 6 or fewer columns, mostly read, no bulk actions, no inline edit, one or two filter dimensions.
PATH-B-SIMPLE.outcome: Fixed columns. Search, one filter, and sort. 25 per page. Vertical scroll only: the page scrolls and the header sticks to the page, with no sideways scroll. One density.

PATH-C.name: Form (Create/Edit)
PATH-C.condition: User is creating a new item, editing an existing item, or completing a workflow/multi-step process.
PATH-C.outcome: Use the Form pattern. Complexity (simple/medium/complex) is decided by field count via PATH-C-SIMPLE / PATH-C-MEDIUM / PATH-C-COMPLEX.

PATH-C-COMPLEX.outcome: Tabs OR 2 columns with sections. Group related fields under section headers (e.g. event creation: left = basic info, right = advanced settings).

PATH-C-MEDIUM.outcome: Single column OR 2 columns. Group related inputs with section headers (e.g. an address group: street, city, state, zip). Space within a section: the 24px scale step (`gap-6`) between fields, the 40px step (`gap-10`) between sections.

PATH-C-SIMPLE.outcome: Single column, stack vertically. No grouping needed. Space between fields: the 24px scale step (`gap-6` in Tailwind).

PATH-COMPOSITION-CHECK-FIRST.name: Check for a Direct Fit First
PATH-COMPOSITION-CHECK-FIRST.condition: A feature brief names its own product-specific job (e.g. "approval queue", "impersonate a user") rather than one of the five container types.
PATH-COMPOSITION-CHECK-FIRST.outcome: Translate the brief into a plain job-to-be-done and re-check it against the SKILL.md decision tree before assuming it needs new structure. Most briefs that sound novel because of their product-specific name are a direct fit for an existing path once translated.

PATH-COMPOSITION-COMBINE.name: Combine Existing Patterns Before Inventing a Third
PATH-COMPOSITION-COMBINE.condition: A brief needs more than one container type's job done at once (e.g. browse-and-approve, multi-step form with a review step, bulk edit from a list).
PATH-COMPOSITION-COMBINE.outcome: Compose the existing container types that each cover part of the job (e.g. PATH-B + PATH-D for an approval queue; PATH-C + PATH-E for a form with a review step) instead of designing one bespoke hybrid container. If you can't name which existing pattern is doing each part of the job, that's the signal to check PATH-COMPOSITION-INVENT-LAST instead.

PATH-COMPOSITION-INVENT-LAST.name: Invent New Structure Only As a Last Resort, and Say So
PATH-COMPOSITION-INVENT-LAST.condition: The job doesn't fit any existing container type directly (PATH-COMPOSITION-CHECK-FIRST) or as a composition of existing ones (PATH-COMPOSITION-COMBINE).
PATH-COMPOSITION-INVENT-LAST.outcome: Build new structure, but name which existing patterns were considered and why they didn't fit — the same reasoning vois_report_pattern_gap asks for, called if available, stated in your own output if not. A new pattern invented this way is a one-off for the brief in front of you, not automatically a new entry in this skill; promoting it to a sixth container type requires the same deliberate review (SKILL.md + patterns-rules.json) every existing path already had.

PATH-COND-ACCORDION-EXCLUSIVE.name: Cascading Accordion/Expansion
PATH-COND-ACCORDION-EXCLUSIVE.condition: A layout contains multiple expandable/accordion forms.
PATH-COND-ACCORDION-EXCLUSIVE.outcome: Only one form can remain expanded at a time. Auto-collapse the previously expanded one when the user opens a new one.

PATH-COND-CALC-TABLE-ROWS.name: Simple Calculation Tables
PATH-COND-CALC-TABLE-ROWS.condition: A calculation dynamically updates a final value from inline input fields and dropdowns (e.g. quantity × unit price).
PATH-COND-CALC-TABLE-ROWS.outcome: Use a simple table layout: header row acts as the field label, inline inputs and dropdowns, and never stack more than 4 rows.

PATH-COND-PARENT-CHILD.name: Parent/Child Input Dependencies
PATH-COND-PARENT-CHILD.condition: A group of related inputs has a conditional relationship — a child input's valid options or availability depend on a parent input's value.
PATH-COND-PARENT-CHILD.outcome: Disable the affected child inputs until the parent input is updated/selected with a valid value. Show them disabled but visible, not hidden, so the relationship stays legible. Route the explanation to righter skill.

PATH-COND-PRIMARY-BUTTON.name: Primary Button State
PATH-COND-PRIMARY-BUTTON.condition: A form has a primary submit action gated on required fields.
PATH-COND-PRIMARY-BUTTON.outcome: The primary button is disabled until all required fields have been filled with valid responses. Route the disabled-state tooltip (e.g. "Fill in all required fields to continue") to righter skill.

PATH-D.name: Dialog / Bottom Sheet
PATH-D.condition: Single quick input needed (amount, selection, confirmation). Simple confirmation (yes/no, approve/reject). Dropdown selection, especially on mobile.
PATH-D.outcome: Desktop: modal dialog, centered, backdrop dims content behind. Mobile: bottom sheet, slides up from bottom, at most 90dvh (DS-RESPONSIVE-008). Never use a bottom sheet if text input/keyboard is required — that is a full-screen form (DS-RESPONSIVE-009). Which container to use: PATH-D-1 to PATH-D-5. Footer button placement: primary right, secondary the 20px scale step (`gap-5`) left of primary, optional tertiary on the left.

PATH-D-1.name: Container 1: confirm
PATH-D-1.condition: One yes or no, a destructive or consequential confirmation, or one pick, and the user needs nothing else from the page to decide.
PATH-D-1.outcome: AlertDialog when the action is destructive or has consequences, otherwise a small Dialog (--width-dialog-sm). The body is one or two sentences. On phone it is a bottom sheet. First focus follows DS-A11Y-020. If none of this fits, go to PATH-D-2.

PATH-D-2.name: Container 2: form dialog
PATH-D-2.condition: One task with one to four stacked fields, and the user does not need the page behind it.
PATH-D-2.outcome: A small Dialog (--width-dialog-sm), single column, two footer buttons at most (DS-MODAL-005). On phone, any text field makes it a full-screen form (DS-RESPONSIVE-009). If it needs more room or more fields, go to PATH-D-3.

PATH-D-3.name: Container 3: large dialog
PATH-D-3.condition: One task whose content needs more width: a textarea or a short list, still a single column.
PATH-D-3.outcome: A large Dialog (--width-dialog-lg). Two-column layouts do not go in a dialog (PATH-FIELD-COLUMNS). On phone it is a full-screen form (DS-RESPONSIVE-009). If it has more than four fields, go to PATH-D-4.

PATH-D-4.name: Container 4: side peek
PATH-D-4.condition: The task touches five to eight fields, or the user needs the page behind it while they work (to compare, copy a value or pick rows).
PATH-D-4.outcome: A right-anchored Sheet (vois-components JOB-OVERLAY-INTERACTION). When the user must keep working in the page, use it as a peek: no scrim and no inert background, so the page stays usable. Otherwise it is a modal Sheet with a scrim. On phone it is full screen (DS-PANEL-002).

PATH-D-5.name: Container 5: page
PATH-D-5.condition: More than eight fields, tabs, a timeline, related records, a long form, or more than one step.
PATH-D-5.outcome: A full page, reached from an Open action in the overlay. Never a bigger dialog, and never a stack of dialogs: a flow with steps is a page (DS-MODAL-006).

PATH-D-SIZE.name: Dialog width
PATH-D-SIZE.condition: Choosing the width of a desktop Dialog or AlertDialog.
PATH-D-SIZE.outcome: Two tiers, both maximums, and every dialog is a single column. Small (--width-dialog-sm): confirmations, AlertDialogs, typed confirmation, and dialogs with one or a few stacked fields. Large (--width-dialog-lg): dialogs whose content needs the extra width, such as a textarea or a short list. Two-column layouts go on pages, not in dialogs. On mobile, text-input dialogs are full modals and the tiers do not apply.

PATH-DENSITY-DENSE.name: Dense Layout
PATH-DENSITY-DENSE.condition: Power user or admin doing this repeatedly; scanning or comparing many rows at once; screen real estate at a premium relative to how much needs to be visible (admin data grids, financial/analytics tables, dashboards, log/audit views).
PATH-DENSITY-DENSE.outcome: Lean toward the tighter end of the spacing scale (--space-4/-8/-12 between related items), more columns/metrics visible without scrolling, smaller non-body type sizes where DS-TYPOGRAPHY still allows it.

PATH-DENSITY-PRODUCT.name: Product setting for density
PATH-DENSITY-PRODUCT.condition: A product sets `workbench` or `relaxed`, and a page already has its tier from PATH-PAGE-DENSITY-MAP.
PATH-DENSITY-PRODUCT.outcome: The setting moves a page's tier by one step. Workbench: Standard becomes Dense. Relaxed: Dense becomes Standard. Spacious never moves. A product that sets nothing keeps the tier the template gives. Then PATH-PAGE-DENSITY-TOUCH applies: when the primary input is not a fine pointer, Dense becomes Standard. So the setting only changes a page when a fine pointer is present. Grid, margins, gutters, columns and panel widths ignore the setting.

PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS.name: Spacious Layout
PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS.condition: Low-frequency, high-stakes, or attention-focusing moment — onboarding/first-run, empty states, a destructive-confirmation dialog, marketing/landing surfaces, a single critical rarely-seen decision point.
PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS.outcome: Lean toward the looser end of the spacing scale (--space-32/-48 and up), fewer things visible at once, more whitespace around the one thing that matters. Optimize for making one decision unmistakable, not for efficiency.

PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD.name: Standard Layout
PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD.condition: Default for most product surfaces — forms, settings pages, typical list/detail views — when neither PATH-DENSITY-DENSE nor PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS's conditions apply.
PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD.outcome: Lean toward the mid spacing scale (--space-16/-24), the values forms.md and settings-pages.md already specify. This is the correct default absent a specific reason to use dense or spacious.

PATH-E.name: Detail Page (Read-Only / View State)
PATH-E.condition: User is viewing a single record in read-only mode. No editing at this level (editing happens on a dedicated form page). User might click through to edit on a separate page.
PATH-E.outcome: Header: breadcrumb above H1 title, close/back button top right if in a modal. Body: groups of related data stacked vertically, each group as label + value, status indicators/badges where relevant. Actions: no primary action in view-only state; an "Edit" link/button navigates to the form page if editing is available. Mobile: stacked single column, no horizontal grouping.

PATH-F.name: Pricing Page
PATH-F.condition: User is showing what a product costs and helping a buyer choose a plan. Billing unit is flat, seat-based, usage-based, hybrid, or consumer subscription, with 1 to 4 real tiers.
PATH-F.outcome: Use the Pricing Page pattern. Billing model picks the sub-decision (PATH-F-FLAT-1 through PATH-F-CONSUMER-PAYWALL). Universal rules (PATH-PRICE-U*) apply to every pricing page. Tier-count rules (PATH-PRICE-T*) apply to layout. Model-specific rules (S, X, H, C) apply per sub-decision.

PATH-F-CONSUMER-PAYWALL.condition: Consumer subscription on iOS or in-app paywall.
PATH-F-CONSUMER-PAYWALL.outcome: Plan cards, trial timeline, CTA that agrees with post-trial price, Restore Purchases, Terms, Privacy. Timing and placement route to conversion-patterns. See PATH-PRICE-C2 to C5, C8, C11.

PATH-F-CONSUMER-WEB.condition: Consumer subscription on a web page (individual, family, student).
PATH-F-CONSUMER-WEB.outcome: Selectable plan cards with a clear selected state and one Continue button. Name family plans by accounts or devices. Show monthly equivalent and real charge. See PATH-PRICE-C1, C2, C6.

PATH-F-FLAT-1.condition: Flat price, one plan (no seats, no meter).
PATH-F-FLAT-1.outcome: Single centered card: price with unit and period, 4 to 8 numeric features, one CTA. See PATH-PRICE-T1. Add a small secondary path for large buyers.

PATH-F-HYBRID.condition: Seat fee plus included usage plus overage.
PATH-F-HYBRID.outcome: Cards show base price and allowance. A calculator (plan, seats, usage, add-ons, total) shows the real bill with monthly and annual totals. See PATH-PRICE-H1 to H4.

PATH-F-SEAT-1.outcome: Single card with per-seat price, included seats, and a seat quantity control (minus and plus around a number) or an input if count changes the price. See PATH-PRICE-T1, PATH-PRICE-S1 to S5.

PATH-F-SEAT-3.outcome: Cards side by side, highlight the middle (or the paid tier when there are 2). Per-seat price with period, included seats, caps disclosed. See PATH-PRICE-T2, T3, S1 to S7.

PATH-F-SEAT-4.outcome: Four cards with short bullets plus a comparison table below. Enterprise shows Custom. Define seat types that bill differently. See PATH-PRICE-T4, S4, S6, U11.

PATH-F-USAGE-1.condition: Usage-based, one plan and one rate.
PATH-F-USAGE-1.outcome: Single card plus an estimator: slider with number input, rate table, itemized total labeled estimated. See PATH-PRICE-X1 to X6.

PATH-F-USAGE-PAYG.outcome: Calculator-first page: slider plus input, live rate table with the active tier highlighted, itemized breakdown, big estimated total, and a note on custom pricing for large volume. See PATH-PRICE-X1 to X5, X10, X11.

PATH-F-USAGE-TIERED.condition: Usage-based, 2 to 4 plans, each with an included allowance and overage.
PATH-F-USAGE-TIERED.outcome: Plan cards show base price and allowance in the buyer's unit. A calculator below recommends a plan from the input and shows overage separately. See PATH-PRICE-X2, X7, X8.

PATH-FIELD-ADDRESS-ORDER.name: Address order
PATH-FIELD-ADDRESS-ORDER.outcome: Country, address line 1, address line 2, city, then state or province and postal code as a pair. Country goes first because it decides which fields appear and how they are labelled. Changing country re-labels and re-validates without clearing typed values. In settings, line 2 is a visible optional field. In short flows it may collapse behind an "Add apartment, suite" link.

PATH-FIELD-ADDRESS-PAIRS.name: Address pairs and autofill
PATH-FIELD-ADDRESS-PAIRS.outcome: State or province at default width pairs with postal code at `--width-field-narrow`. City sits alone. Never put three fields in one row. Set `autocomplete` on every field (address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, address-level1, postal-code, country).

PATH-FIELD-CHAT-INPUT.name: AI chat input
PATH-FIELD-CHAT-INPUT.condition: The user types a message into an AI or chat thread.
PATH-FIELD-CHAT-INPUT.outcome: One textarea using the same auto-growing pattern. It starts at `--chat-input-min-lines`, grows to `--chat-input-max-lines`, then scrolls inside. The composer is anchored to the bottom of the thread, so growth pushes upward and the send control stays aligned to the composer's bottom edge. It fills its container and is not capped by `--width-field-max` or `--width-form-max`, because the thread column sets its width. The chat container uses `dvh` so it tracks the mobile keyboard. Keep an accessible name even when there is no visible label.

PATH-FIELD-COLUMN-GAP.name: Column gap
PATH-FIELD-COLUMN-GAP.condition: Two columns sit side by side.
PATH-FIELD-COLUMN-GAP.outcome: `gap-6` by default and `gap-10` when the DENSITY dial is 3 or lower. Vertical gaps between fields and sections are already set in `forms.md` (`gap-6` and `gap-10`).

PATH-FIELD-COLUMNS.name: Two columns at most
PATH-FIELD-COLUMNS.outcome: Use at most two columns. Pair only related fields of similar length, such as first and last name, or state and postal code. Address line 1, email, phone, and textareas always sit alone. Dialogs are always one column (`[PATH-D-SIZE]`). Visual order equals tab order.

PATH-FIELD-CONTAINER.name: Form container
PATH-FIELD-CONTAINER.outcome: Cap the form container at `--width-form-max`. The layout holds down to `--width-viewport-min` with no horizontal scroll.

PATH-FIELD-EMAIL.name: Email
PATH-FIELD-EMAIL.condition: An email field appears in a regular form.
PATH-FIELD-EMAIL.outcome: Default width, email keypad and `autocomplete="email"` on mobile. In account settings it follows `[PATH-SET-IDENTITY-FIELD]` instead.

PATH-FIELD-LABEL.name: Optional marking
PATH-FIELD-LABEL.outcome: If most fields are required, mark the optional ones "(optional)" instead of marking every required one. Label placement and style are already covered.

PATH-FIELD-NAME.name: Name
PATH-FIELD-NAME.outcome: First name and last name as a pair. Use one full-name field only when the product treats the name as a single string.

PATH-FIELD-OTP-INPUT.name: One-time code
PATH-FIELD-OTP-INPUT.condition: The user enters a fixed-length code, such as an email or SMS verification code.
PATH-FIELD-OTP-INPUT.outcome: Use InputOTP with one cell per character, behaving as one field: one tab stop, paste fills every cell, backspace moves back, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, and a numeric keypad when the code is digits only. Keep a visible label. Cells share the row equally with `gap-2`, cap at `size-12`, and shrink to fit down to `--width-viewport-min`. The group caps at `--width-field-max`. The group is one hit area of at least `--hit-area-min` tall, and a tap on any cell focuses the first empty one, so cells can shrink visually without losing the target. The error state puts an icon and text under the group and puts every cell in the error style.

PATH-FIELD-PHONE-CONTROL.name: Phone as one control
PATH-FIELD-PHONE-CONTROL.outcome: One joined control with a country selector and a number input on a single row sharing one label. The selector is a Combobox with a fixed width of `w-24` and the number input takes the rest. The row stays on one line at `--width-viewport-min`. The whole control caps at `--width-field-max`. Closed, the selector shows the flag and dial code, and the open list shows country name and dial code with frequently used countries pinned first. The default follows the user's locale.

PATH-FIELD-PHONE-INPUT.name: Number entry
PATH-FIELD-PHONE-INPUT.condition: The user types a phone number.
PATH-FIELD-PHONE-INPUT.outcome: Format as they type using the selected country's pattern, show a telephone keypad on mobile, and store in international format.

PATH-FIELD-TEXTAREA-AUTOSIZE.name: Auto-growing text areas
PATH-FIELD-TEXTAREA-AUTOSIZE.condition: A multi-line text field, such as notes, a description, or feedback.
PATH-FIELD-TEXTAREA-AUTOSIZE.outcome: It grows with its content using CSS `field-sizing: content`, never JavaScript. It starts at `--textarea-min-lines`, stops growing at `--textarea-max-lines`, and scrolls inside after that. The CSS pattern, the required width setting, and the fallback are in `[DS-LAYOUT-FIELD-001]` to `[DS-LAYOUT-FIELD-004]`.

PATH-FIELD-WIDTH.name: Field width tiers
PATH-FIELD-WIDTH.outcome: Single-line inputs and selects fill their column up to `--width-field-max`. Short fixed-format values (postal code, state or province code, expiry, security code) cap at `--width-field-narrow` and never stretch. Multi-line textareas may fill up to `--width-form-max` and grow in height per `[PATH-FIELD-TEXTAREA-AUTOSIZE]`. Single-line fields never exceed `--width-field-max`.

PATH-FIELD-WRAP.name: Wrapping
PATH-FIELD-WRAP.outcome: Two columns become one when the form's container is narrower than the `sm` breakpoint value (`37.5em`). Use a container query so forms inside drawers and side panels wrap correctly. Source order is preserved. The phone control and the one-time-code group never split.

PATH-G.name: Marketing Page
PATH-G.condition: User is showing what a product or business offers to people who are not yet using it: a landing page, homepage, or product marketing page. Not a pricing page (PATH-F) and not product UI.
PATH-G.outcome: Use the Marketing Page pattern. Every feature block is the same stack: image, short title, one or two sentences, one link. Sections are far apart and text inside them is tight. PATH-G-* rules apply. Words go to righter (slot limits), type and spacing to vois-tokens (DS-MKT). These are taste rules for marketing surfaces, not general laws.

PATH-G-ALIGN.name: Left-align by default
PATH-G-ALIGN.condition: Text and block alignment on a marketing page.
PATH-G-ALIGN.outcome: Left-align. Center only the closing call to action.

PATH-G-BLOCKS.name: Three blocks max
PATH-G-BLOCKS.condition: Any row or stack of blocks on a marketing page.
PATH-G-BLOCKS.outcome: No more than three blocks. If there are more, group them (five programs become three audience tiles) and link to the detail. Three is a ceiling, not a target. Blocks should still differ in size or emphasis.

PATH-G-CTA.name: One primary button per view
PATH-G-CTA.condition: Buttons and calls to action on a marketing page.
PATH-G-CTA.outcome: One primary button per view. A secondary button is allowed in the hero only. Repeat the primary call to action at most twice on a page (hero and close). Everything else is a plain link.

PATH-G-DETAIL.name: Detail goes behind a link
PATH-G-DETAIL.condition: Full schedules, bios, long FAQs, or any long list on a marketing page.
PATH-G-DETAIL.outcome: Put the full version on its own page. Show a taste on the page: about 5 schedule rows, one coach sentence, 3 questions, each with a link to the rest.

PATH-G-DIVIDERS.name: No dividers
PATH-G-DIVIDERS.condition: Sections on a marketing page that blur together.
PATH-G-DIVIDERS.outcome: Do not use hairlines, boxes, or borders to separate sections. Increase the section gap instead (DS-MKT-006).

PATH-G-FOOTER.name: Footer at heading scale
PATH-G-FOOTER.condition: The footer of a marketing page.
PATH-G-FOOTER.outcome: Repeat the nav as large links at h2 size plus the wordmark. Small print stays small.

PATH-G-SECTION.name: One idea per section
PATH-G-SECTION.condition: Any section on a marketing page.
PATH-G-SECTION.outcome: One heading, one block of content, one link. If a section needs two headings, it is two sections.

PATH-G-TILE.name: Image tile first
PATH-G-TILE.condition: A feature block on a marketing page.
PATH-G-TILE.outcome: Large rounded image tile, then a title, then one or two sentences, then one link. Tiles are at least 300px tall on mobile.

PATH-H.name: Questionnaire
PATH-H.condition: The user answers a series of questions that someone else wrote (survey, intake, assessment, feedback form). They are not editing their own records.
PATH-H.outcome: Read references/questionnaires.md. Show one question per screen. Apply PATH-H-1 to PATH-H-5. Dense desktop forms stay in PATH-C.

PATH-H-1.name: Layout
PATH-H-1.condition: Choosing how many questions to show at once.
PATH-H-1.outcome: One question per screen. Group 2 to 3 simple questions on one page only when the survey has 10 questions or fewer. Put a full-width Next in a sticky bar in the thumb zone. Centre the content at 640px max from 768px up. A grid of questions is never the default.

PATH-H-2.name: Component by question properties
PATH-H-2.condition: A question needs a component. Check these properties in order. The first match wins.
PATH-H-2.outcome: 1. Long answer over 120 characters: LongTextbox. 2. Short answer: OpenText. For a typed value (email, phone, number) use vois-fields. 3. Several statements share one scale: accordion, one statement at a time, 5 per group at most. 4. 11 points (0 to 10): slider with word labels. 5. 5 points: Likert, horizontal. 7 points: Likert, vertical. 6. Order matters: rank (press and hold drag sort, with up and down buttons). 6 items or fewer rank all. 7 to 12 rank the top 3. Over 12, do not rank. 7. Multiple answers: CheckboxCard. 8. Single answer: RadioCard up to 7 options, RadioListRow for 8 to 12, searchable list over 12.

PATH-H-3.name: Flow and progress
PATH-H-3.outcome: Next is explicit. Never auto-advance. Show a 4px bar plus text such as Question 3 of 12. Progress counts required questions on the respondent's path. If branching would change the total, use section progress. Back restores answers. Save each answer on change and show a quiet Saved state. End with a Review screen that lists every answer with an Edit link.

PATH-H-4.name: Required and errors
PATH-H-4.condition: A question is required, optional, or fails a check.
PATH-H-4.outcome: Mark every question Required or Optional in words. After a failed Next show a top banner with links, a specific inline error under each bad question, a 2px error border, and move focus to the first error. Fix clears the error at once. Put the error above the input so the keyboard cannot cover it.

PATH-H-5.name: Prefill and drafts
PATH-H-5.condition: A question has a value from a profile, an earlier answer, a link, or an AI guess.
PATH-H-5.outcome: Follow FIELD-PREFILL in vois-fields. Show prefill with its source and let the respondent edit it. A low confidence or AI guess is a suggestion chip under a blank field, never a filled value. Never submit a prefilled value the respondent did not see. A link that would overwrite a saved draft asks first.

PATH-H-6.name: Poll and quiz results
PATH-H-6.condition: The respondent should see how others answered a choice question, or whether their answer was correct.
PATH-H-6.outcome: Set reveal on a single_select or multi_select question. Show results only after the answer. Keep option order. Mark the correct option with an icon and words. Round single-choice percents to 100. Hide numbers under 10 votes. See PATH-H-6 in references/questionnaires.md.

PATH-NATIVE-BACK.name: Back and close on phone
PATH-NATIVE-BACK.condition: A phone screen opens another screen.
PATH-NATIVE-BACK.outcome: Drill-down pushes a new level and shows a back control at the top left (PATH-PAGE-LEVELS). Do not replace the system back gesture with a custom swipe. A full-screen modal shows a close control at the top left, and that is a close, not a back. The bottom tab bar may stay on a detail screen.

PATH-NATIVE-DISMISS.name: Sheets always have a visible way out
PATH-NATIVE-DISMISS.condition: A sheet can be dismissed by swiping down.
PATH-NATIVE-DISMISS.outcome: Every sheet shows a visible close control or Cancel. Swiping down is extra, never the only way out. A sheet with unsaved edits ignores a swipe down and asks to discard (PATH-PAGE-VIEW-EDIT). A nonmodal sheet with detents keeps its close control at every detent.

PATH-NATIVE-FORM-SHEET.name: Form in a modal sheet
PATH-NATIVE-FORM-SHEET.condition: A form opens as a modal sheet on a phone.
PATH-NATIVE-FORM-SHEET.outcome: The tall modal sheet is how the full screen overlay in PATH-PAGE-OVERLAY looks on iOS: the parent shows above it and the title is centered in a top bar. Close or Cancel sits on the left. A named commit sits on the right (Add, Create, Save). The commit stays disabled until the form can be saved. It is never an action sheet (PATH-D). Labels come from righter.

PATH-NATIVE-REFRESH.name: Pull to refresh
PATH-NATIVE-REFRESH.condition: A list can be refreshed by pulling down.
PATH-NATIVE-REFRESH.outcome: Use pull to refresh only at the top of a list sorted by recent content. Never on a map, a canvas or other content that pans. Every pull to refresh also has a visible refresh control for fine pointers. Show the result briefly (a toast or a pill).

PATH-NATIVE-SHEET-KIND.name: Modal or nonmodal sheet
PATH-NATIVE-SHEET-KIND.condition: Something opens over the page on a phone.
PATH-NATIVE-SHEET-KIND.outcome: If the user still needs the page behind it (a map, a list they keep using), open a nonmodal sheet with detents and no scrim, and keep the page usable. If they do not (a form, a confirmation, a pick), open a modal sheet or an alert with a scrim. A long task, or one with its own URL, is a full screen. From tablet up, a nonmodal sheet becomes a side panel and a modal sheet becomes a dialog or popover, as PATH-PAGE-OVERLAY says. Nothing opens over a popover except an alert.

PATH-NATIVE-SWIPE-ROW.name: One swipe action per row
PATH-NATIVE-SWIPE-ROW.condition: A list row has a swipe action.
PATH-NATIVE-SWIPE-ROW.outcome: Reveal at most one action on the trailing swipe. If it deletes or removes, it is red and has a text label. Never stack two or more. A swipe is never the only path: the same action is also on a visible menu or on the detail screen. Keep horizontal swipe handlers away from the screen edges, where back gestures start. A row inside a horizontally scrolling area has no swipe action.

PATH-PAGE.name: Page template
PATH-PAGE.condition: The task is a whole page or screen layout (what regions it has, how it changes at each width, how people get in and out of it), not one container. Examples: a landing page, a dashboard, a list page, a record page, a settings page.
PATH-PAGE.outcome: Pick the page by level and product type from data/page-templates.json, then follow the PATH rules it routes to. The template gives the skeleton. The routed rules give the content and win on any difference. Cross-cutting PATH-PAGE-* rules cover breakpoints, navigation, density at each width, overlays, button order and view to edit.

PATH-PAGE-ARTICLE.name: Blog post
PATH-PAGE-ARTICLE.condition: Level 3 (Detail), marketing. One long read. Built for comfortable reading, then a next step.
PATH-PAGE-ARTICLE.outcome: Use the Blog post skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS. Phone: Header and hero image full width. Contents fold into one row at the top. Share icons move under the article. Desktop: Share icons on the left, article in the middle at about 680px, contents and tags on the right.

PATH-PAGE-BLOG-INDEX.name: Blog index
PATH-PAGE-BLOG-INDEX.condition: Level 2 (Index), marketing. Lists articles and helps readers find the ones they care about. Also grows the newsletter.
PATH-PAGE-BLOG-INDEX.outcome: Use the Blog index skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS. Phone: Featured post on top, then the New list, then one post per row. Chips scroll sideways. Newsletter signup stacks. Desktop: Featured post takes two thirds with the New list beside it. Posts three across.

PATH-PAGE-BREAKPOINTS.name: Page widths
PATH-PAGE-BREAKPOINTS.condition: Any template is drawn or checked at a width.
PATH-PAGE-BREAKPOINTS.outcome: Phone is below md (768px). Tablet is md up to lg (768px to 1023px). Desktop is lg and up (1024px). Check every template at all three. For grids, phone splits in two at 600px (the `sm` grid class), so check phone at 360px and at 600px as well. Grid and panel rules live in `vois-tokens` (`DS-GRID-*` and `DS-PANEL-*`). A native Android layout is also checked at `expanded` (840px). It is a breakpoint token, not a grid class.

PATH-PAGE-BROWSE.name: Browse grid
PATH-PAGE-BROWSE.condition: Level 2 (Index), consumer. A browsable grid of items. People narrow it down, then pick one.
PATH-PAGE-BROWSE.outcome: Use the Browse grid skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: Two cards per row. Filter and Sort stay pinned top right above the grid. Filter opens a full height sheet. The apply button shows the result count. Desktop: Filter sidebar on the left with four groups. Four cards per row.

PATH-PAGE-BUTTON-ORDER.name: Button order
PATH-PAGE-BUTTON-ORDER.condition: Two or more buttons sit side by side.
PATH-PAGE-BUTTON-ORDER.outcome: Primary is rightmost. Secondary sits to its left, then tertiary or ghost to the left of that. When buttons stack on phone, primary is on top. One primary per group. In a step flow, Back sits alone at the far left of the footer, and the buttons on the right follow the same order (Skip, then primary). Buttons in a footer or sticky bar are right-aligned with the 20px gap step between them (16 to 24px is the allowed range), never spread to the two edges or stretched to fill the bar.

PATH-PAGE-CASE-STUDY.name: Case study
PATH-PAGE-CASE-STUDY.condition: Level 3 (Detail), marketing. One customer story told as a problem, a fix, and a result. Numbers go first.
PATH-PAGE-CASE-STUDY.outcome: Use the Case study skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS. Phone: Breadcrumb hides. Stats stack one per row. Company facts fold into a two by two block above the story. Desktop: Header text beside a photo. Three stats in a row. Company facts in a left column and the story capped near 680px.

PATH-PAGE-COLLECTION.name: Collection table
PATH-PAGE-COLLECTION.condition: Level 2 (Index), saas. A list of records people scan, filter, and act on in bulk.
PATH-PAGE-COLLECTION.outcome: Use the Collection table skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: Rows turn into stacked cards with the name, status, and one line of detail. Filter and Sort stay pinned top right. Filter opens a full screen Drawer because filters include text fields. New record becomes a floating button and opens full screen, since it has text inputs. Desktop: Full table with checkboxes. Applied filters show as chips under the toolbar. Preview panel on the right.

PATH-PAGE-CONTACT.name: Contact sales
PATH-PAGE-CONTACT.condition: Level 4 (Utility), marketing. A short form for people ready to talk to a person. It should feel safe and quick.
PATH-PAGE-CONTACT.outcome: Use the Contact sales skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: Heading, then the form, then the reasons to trust you. Fields are one column. Desktop: Heading, benefits, and trust badges on the left. Form card on the right.

PATH-PAGE-CUSTOMERS.name: Customer stories
PATH-PAGE-CUSTOMERS.condition: Level 2 (Index), marketing. The proof page. It collects testimonials and case studies so visitors can find one that looks like them.
PATH-PAGE-CUSTOMERS.outcome: Use the Customer stories skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS. Phone: Hero stats sit under the heading. Chips scroll sideways. Story cards and quotes run one per row. Desktop: Hero text beside a stat list. Featured story split into image and text. Story grid three across. Quote wall two across.

PATH-PAGE-DASHBOARD.name: Dashboard
PATH-PAGE-DASHBOARD.condition: Level 1 (Hub), saas. The landing page inside a SaaS product. It answers what changed and what needs attention.
PATH-PAGE-DASHBOARD.outcome: Use the Dashboard skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-DENSE. Phone: Sidebar becomes a bottom bar with four tabs and More. Metrics go two across. Chart and activity stack. The table turns into stacked rows: name as the title, with status and the other values under it. Nothing is dropped. Desktop: Full sidebar. Four metrics in a row. Chart takes two thirds with activity beside it. Full table.

PATH-PAGE-DATAGRID.name: Data grid
PATH-PAGE-DATAGRID.condition: Level 2 (Index), saas. A dense, spreadsheet-like table for people who live in it all day. Sorting, column control, and bulk edits matter more than looks.
PATH-PAGE-DATAGRID.outcome: Use the Data grid skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-DENSE. Phone: The grid keeps every column and scrolls sideways inside its card, with the selection box and name pinned on the left. Never hide columns on a table (PATH-B-NARROW). Filter and Sort stay pinned top right as two buttons. Selecting rows shows a bar above the list with one Actions button. Desktop: All columns, a Columns menu, row height control, export, and a bulk action bar above the header when rows are checked. Scrolls sideways when columns outrun the width, with the name column pinned.

PATH-PAGE-DENSITY-MAP.name: Density tier by page
PATH-PAGE-DENSITY-MAP.condition: Choosing a density tier for a whole page.
PATH-PAGE-DENSITY-MAP.outcome: Marketing and landing pages, for consumer apps and SaaS products alike: Spacious, and always looser than the product itself. Pricing, contact, consumer app screens, forms, settings and everyday lists: Standard. Dashboards, analytics tables, data grids, inboxes: Dense with a fine pointer.

PATH-PAGE-DENSITY-TOUCH.name: Dense is for pointers only
PATH-PAGE-DENSITY-TOUCH.condition: A Dense page is shown while the primary input is not a fine pointer (CSS `(pointer: fine)` does not match), at any width.
PATH-PAGE-DENSITY-TOUCH.outcome: Rows go back to --table-row-h-regular. Targets reach --hit-area-min. Gaps between blocks go up one step. Fewer rows fit on screen, and that is accepted. Unknown input counts as touch. A phone-width window with a mouse can stay Dense, and its layout still follows width (PATH-B-NARROW). An iPad with a trackpad still reports a touch primary input, so it stays at regular rows.

PATH-PAGE-FEATURE.name: Feature page
PATH-PAGE-FEATURE.condition: Level 1 (Hub), marketing. Explains one part of the product in depth. It sits between the home page and the signup.
PATH-PAGE-FEATURE.outcome: Use the Feature page skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS. Phone: Everything stacks. Each feature row shows its screenshot first, then the text. Integrations show four across. Desktop: Feature rows alternate screenshot and text side by side. Integrations eight across.

PATH-PAGE-FEED.name: Feed home
PATH-PAGE-FEED.condition: Level 1 (Hub), consumer. The home screen of a consumer app. It scrolls without end and mixes posts, media, and suggestions.
PATH-PAGE-FEED.outcome: Use the Feed home skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: Top bar plus a bottom tab bar with five items. The feed fills the width. The right rail goes away, so move trending and suggestions into a Search tab. Desktop: Three columns: labeled nav, feed, and a right rail with search, trending, and people to follow.

PATH-PAGE-INVOICES.name: Invoices and billing
PATH-PAGE-INVOICES.condition: Level 4 (Utility), saas. A read-mostly table. People come here to find one invoice, download it, or check what they owe.
PATH-PAGE-INVOICES.outcome: Use the Invoices and billing skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: Summary cards go two across. Each invoice is a stacked row: number as the title, with date, amount, and a status badge under it. Download moves into the row menu. Desktop: Four summary cards, then the full table with a PDF button per row and a Download all button.

PATH-PAGE-LEVELS.condition: A product has a dashboard or home, then sections, then single items.
PATH-PAGE-LEVELS.outcome: Number the pages by level: 0 Entry, 1 Hub, 2 Index, 3 Detail, 4 Utility. Each page knows its parent. Back goes up exactly one level. Desktop shows the trail (Dashboard, Section, Item). Phone shows a back control to the parent and the page title.

PATH-PAGE-MARKETING-HOME.name: Marketing home
PATH-PAGE-MARKETING-HOME.condition: Level 0 (Entry), both. The front door. One job: explain the product and get a signup.
PATH-PAGE-MARKETING-HOME.outcome: Use the Marketing home skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS. Phone: Single column. Buttons stack to full width. Logos wrap to three per row. Plans stack, so put the recommended plan first. Footer links sit in two columns. Desktop: Two column hero. Features three across. Split sections put image and text side by side. Five column footer.

PATH-PAGE-NAV.name: App shell navigation by width
PATH-PAGE-NAV.condition: A signed-in SaaS or consumer app has more than one section.
PATH-PAGE-NAV.outcome: Desktop: labeled sidebar. Tablet: icon rail. Phone: bottom tab bar with at most five slots, the last being More. The settings section menu is separate and follows PATH-A. A marketing top bar shows its links at lg and up and folds them into one menu control below that. The signup button stays visible at every width.

PATH-PAGE-ONBOARDING.name: Onboarding steps
PATH-PAGE-ONBOARDING.condition: Level 4 (Utility), both. A short, focused setup of 2 to 5 steps with a 1-2-3 stepper, shown before or just after the first visit. One question group per step, then into the product.
PATH-PAGE-ONBOARDING.outcome: Use the Onboarding steps skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS. Phone: Stepper keeps its three markers but drops the labels and adds one line, Step 2 of 3: Goals. Content is one column. Back and Next sit in a sticky bottom bar with Next filling the width, and Skip is a text link above it. Desktop: Same as tablet with more air around the column. Choice cards go two across. The footer stays under the content, not pinned to the window.

PATH-PAGE-OVERLAY.name: Which overlay opens
PATH-PAGE-OVERLAY.condition: A page action opens something on top of the page.
PATH-PAGE-OVERLAY.outcome: A yes or no, or a pick: modal on desktop, bottom sheet on phone. Any text field: modal on desktop, full screen on phone, never a bottom sheet. Editing or previewing a row: right panel (a Sheet) on tablet and desktop, full screen on phone. Filters: right panel on tablet and desktop, and on phone a full screen Drawer (vois-components JOB-OVERLAY-INTERACTION). Notifications: right panel. Always keep a visible way back, and Escape or the scrim closes it on desktop.

PATH-PAGE-PRICING.name: Pricing
PATH-PAGE-PRICING.condition: Level 1 (Hub), marketing. Helps a visitor pick a plan and commit. It also answers the objections that stop a signup.
PATH-PAGE-PRICING.outcome: Use the Pricing skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: Plans stack one per card. Put the recommended plan first. The comparison table shows one plan at a time, chosen with a row of plan buttons above it. Desktop: Four plan cards in a row with the recommended one outlined heavier. Full comparison table with grouped rows.

PATH-PAGE-PRODUCT.name: Product detail
PATH-PAGE-PRODUCT.condition: Level 3 (Detail), consumer. One item, with everything needed to decide and buy.
PATH-PAGE-PRODUCT.outcome: Use the Product detail skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: Gallery swipes with dots. Details sit in accordions. Price and Add to bag live in a sticky bar at the bottom. Desktop: Thumbnails run down the left of the main image. The buy box is about 380px wide on the right.

PATH-PAGE-RECORD.name: Record detail
PATH-PAGE-RECORD.condition: Level 3 (Detail), saas. One record in a SaaS product, such as a customer, a job, or a service. It shows status and lets people act.
PATH-PAGE-RECORD.outcome: Use the Record detail skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: A back link replaces the breadcrumb. The primary action sits under the title and the rest go in an overflow menu. Tabs scroll sideways. Properties fold into one row. Desktop: Three actions in the header. Properties panel on the right at 300px. Facts go three across.

PATH-PAGE-REPORT.name: Report table
PATH-PAGE-REPORT.condition: Level 3 (Detail), saas. A table that summarizes numbers: a date range, a chart, and rows with a totals line. Mostly read, then exported.
PATH-PAGE-REPORT.outcome: Use the Report table skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-DENSE. Phone: Controls collapse into a date chip and an Options button. The chart shrinks. The table keeps every column, scrolls sideways inside its card, and pins the first column. The page itself never scrolls sideways. Desktop: All columns, a bold totals row at the bottom, and Export in the header.

PATH-PAGE-SETTINGS.name: Settings
PATH-PAGE-SETTINGS.condition: Level 4 (Utility), both. Where people change how the product works for them or their team.
PATH-PAGE-SETTINGS.outcome: Use the Settings skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: The section list moves behind a hamburger at the top of the page, and the page shows one section at a time (PATH-A). Fields are one column. Cancel and Save sit in a sticky bar, right-aligned with 20px between them and Save rightmost. Desktop: Sub navigation list on the left at 200px. Content is capped near 640px so lines stay readable. Save buttons sit at the end of the form.

PATH-PAGE-SORT-FILTER.name: Sort and filter position
PATH-PAGE-SORT-FILTER.condition: A table, list or card grid can be sorted or filtered.
PATH-PAGE-SORT-FILTER.outcome: Pin Filter and Sort to the top right of the table, list or card grid, on the same row as the search field, which sits on the left. Filter is left of Sort, so Sort is the rightmost control. The position is the same at phone, tablet and desktop. On phone they stay on that top row as two compact buttons, not in a bottom bar. Other toolbar controls (Columns, row height, view toggles, Export) sit to the left of Filter. Filter opens a right panel on tablet and desktop and a full screen Drawer on phone (PATH-PAGE-OVERLAY). Where a layout has a persistent filter sidebar, the Filter button still sits top right and shows or hides the sidebar. Applied filters show as dismissible chips under the toolbar. A sortable column header may also sort (PATH-TABLE-SORT), but the Sort button must always exist, because stacked rows and card grids have no column headers. A table that cannot be sorted or filtered, such as a short summary table that links to the full list, has neither control.

PATH-PAGE-SPLIT.name: List with detail pane
PATH-PAGE-SPLIT.condition: Level 3 (Detail), saas. For triage work like an inbox, tickets, or tasks. People move down a list and need the detail without losing their place.
PATH-PAGE-SPLIT.outcome: Use the List with detail pane skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-DENSE. Phone: List only. Tapping a row pushes the detail as its own screen. Compose or Add becomes a floating button. Desktop: List on the left, a wider detail pane on the right, with tabs for overview, activity, and notes.

PATH-PAGE-TABLE-WIDTH.name: Tables at narrow widths
PATH-PAGE-TABLE-WIDTH.condition: A page template contains a table at phone or tablet width.
PATH-PAGE-TABLE-WIDTH.outcome: Do not hide columns. Follow PATH-B-NARROW: four columns or fewer stack as list rows, more scroll sideways inside the table with the first column and header pinned. The page itself never scrolls sideways.

PATH-PAGE-TEAM.name: Members table
PATH-PAGE-TEAM.condition: Level 4 (Utility), saas. A short table inside settings. People are here to invite someone, change a role, or remove someone.
PATH-PAGE-TEAM.outcome: Use the Members table skeleton in data/page-templates.json. Density: PATH-DENSITY-STANDARD. Phone: Each person is a stacked row: avatar and name as the title, with email, role, and status under it. Tapping the row opens the edit panel. Invite stays at the top. Desktop: Sub-nav column on the left. Table with Role dropdown, Joined date, and Status. Active and Invited are grouped under small headers.

PATH-PAGE-VIEW-EDIT.name: View to edit on the same page
PATH-PAGE-VIEW-EDIT.condition: A record page or settings block can be changed.
PATH-PAGE-VIEW-EDIT.outcome: Open in view state. Edit is an explicit action that swaps the same fields to inputs in place. Save and Cancel replace Edit. Leaving with unsaved changes opens a Discard confirmation (bottom sheet on phone). On phone Save sits in a sticky bar.

PATH-PERM-DISABLE-BY-CONDITION.name: Disable Controls by Permission or Condition
PATH-PERM-DISABLE-BY-CONDITION.condition: Content the user cannot update due to an org admin setting or a cascading choice condition (e.g. a workspace admin disabled this setting, the record is archived).
PATH-PERM-DISABLE-BY-CONDITION.outcome: Keep the element visible but disabled, in a view-only/disabled state, so the user can visually map the cause/effect relationship. Route the disabled-state explanation (tooltip or helper text) to righter skill.

PATH-PERM-HIDE-BY-ROLE.name: Hide Page Elements by Role
PATH-PERM-HIDE-BY-ROLE.condition: User role doesn't have permission to see an element (e.g. non-admin viewing a Members section, non-owner viewing Billing, unpermitted user viewing a Delete account button).
PATH-PERM-HIDE-BY-ROLE.outcome: Hide the element entirely — it never renders in the DOM. This is deletion, not disabling. Check role at render time; don't render the element at all.

PATH-PERM-PII-KEEP-OUT.name: Keep personal data out of URLs, titles, file names, and analytics
PATH-PERM-PII-KEEP-OUT.condition: Building a URL, query string, page title, breadcrumb, browser history entry, export file name, or analytics event for a screen that involves a person.
PATH-PERM-PII-KEEP-OUT.outcome: Use opaque IDs, not personal data: `/customers/c_8f2a`, not `/customers/jane.doe@acme.com`. A title or breadcrumb may show a name only on a screen whose job is that person, and never an email, phone number, address, or ID. Name exports by content and date, such as `customers-2026-10-06.csv`. Analytics properties carry IDs, never values (see `metrics-tagging`). For error, toast, and notification copy, see righter `no-pii-in-copy`.

PATH-PERM-PII-MASK.name: Mask personal data by default
PATH-PERM-PII-MASK.condition: A list, table, card, or header shows personal data (email, phone, street address, date of birth, government ID, payment number) to a user whose task doesn't need the full value.
PATH-PERM-PII-MASK.outcome: Show a masked value by default: `j***@acme.com`, `•••• 4821`, last four digits only. A person's name stays visible on a screen whose job is that person (a people list, a profile). Show the full value only to roles that need it, and only through the reveal control (`PATH-PERM-PII-REVEAL`) or on a detail view. A role that never needs it never receives it. Mask on the server, so the full value never reaches the page for roles that can't see it. CSS blur or hiding is not masking. Masked values keep the column width so the layout doesn't jump.

PATH-PERM-PII-REVEAL.name: Reveal a masked value on request
PATH-PERM-PII-REVEAL.condition: A role that is allowed to see a masked value needs the full one.
PATH-PERM-PII-REVEAL.outcome: Put a reveal control on that one field, not on the whole page, and wherever the masked value appears (a list row, a card, a header, or a detail view): an icon Button with a label such as "Show email". The value re-masks when the user leaves the view or after a timeout. Log reveals of high-risk fields (government ID, payment, health data) on the server. Copy to clipboard copies the full value only for roles that may reveal it.

PATH-PRICE-C1.name: Plan choice is radio cards with one Continue button
PATH-PRICE-C1.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
PATH-PRICE-C1.outcome: MasterClass and Quizlet show cards with a clear selected state and one button below. Do not hide prices behind a tap.

PATH-PRICE-C10.name: One line on why it costs money
PATH-PRICE-C10.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
PATH-PRICE-C10.outcome: Halide has a "Why is Halide not free?" block. For indie or small-team apps it earns trust.

PATH-PRICE-C11.name: Placement, timing, and trial-vs-no-trial go to `conversion-patterns`
PATH-PRICE-C11.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
PATH-PRICE-C11.outcome: Placement, timing, and trial-vs-no-trial go to `conversion-patterns`.

PATH-PRICE-C2.name: Show both the monthly equivalent and the real charge
PATH-PRICE-C2.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.

PATH-PRICE-C3.name: Explain the trial as a timeline
PATH-PRICE-C3.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.

PATH-PRICE-C4.name: The CTA and the small print agree
PATH-PRICE-C4.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
PATH-PRICE-C4.outcome: "Start free trial" with "7-day free, then $29.98/year" right under it (Halide). Blue Apron adds a terms checkbox before enabling the button.

PATH-PRICE-C5.name: iOS: always show Restore Purchases, Terms, Privacy
PATH-PRICE-C5.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.

PATH-PRICE-C6.name: Name family plans by who's in them
PATH-PRICE-C6.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
PATH-PRICE-C6.outcome: Deezer: "1 account / 2 accounts / 6 accounts." MasterClass: "1 account, 6 devices."

PATH-PRICE-C7.name: Free vs Pro list when free is real
PATH-PRICE-C7.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
PATH-PRICE-C7.outcome: Tide Guide shows a checklist with two columns. It makes the upgrade feel concrete.

PATH-PRICE-C8.name: Sticky CTAs must not cover a plan
PATH-PRICE-C8.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
PATH-PRICE-C8.outcome: Tide Guide's button sits over the annual plan card in the screen I saw. Test with the smallest supported device.

PATH-PRICE-C9.name: Strikethrough anchors only for real prior prices
PATH-PRICE-C9.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
PATH-PRICE-C9.outcome: Lifesum and Deezer use them. If the higher price was never charged, don't show it. *Ethical rule, not observed.*

PATH-PRICE-H1.name: Show usage per seat
PATH-PRICE-H1.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
PATH-PRICE-H1.outcome: Windsurf: "500 prompt credits / user / month." Buyers multiply by team size. Put the multiplication in the calculator.

PATH-PRICE-H2.name: Calculator order follows how buyers think
PATH-PRICE-H2.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
PATH-PRICE-H2.outcome: Plan, then seats, then usage, then add-ons, then total. GitBook: plan, site count, users, total per month and per year. Teak adds an add-on toggle.

PATH-PRICE-H3.name: Two totals
PATH-PRICE-H3.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.

PATH-PRICE-H4.name: Keep the cards simple, put the math in the calculator
PATH-PRICE-H4.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
PATH-PRICE-H4.outcome: Cards show the base price and allowance. The calculator shows the real bill. Don't cram both into one card.

PATH-PRICE-S1.name: Price per seat per month, with the period

PATH-PRICE-S3.name: Add a quantity control on the card when seat count changes the price
PATH-PRICE-S3.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
PATH-PRICE-S3.outcome: Mistral puts "$50/mo, 2 users" with +/- on the Team card. GitBook uses a number input and shows a running total. Show monthly and annual totals.

PATH-PRICE-S4.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
