PATH-PRICE-S5.outcome: "Up to 50 members" (Height), "max 15 seats" (Lyssna). Buyers hit these walls later and feel tricked if you hid them.

PATH-PRICE-S6.name: Volume discounts live on the Enterprise card
PATH-PRICE-S6.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).

PATH-PRICE-S7.name: If the free tier has unlimited seats, say it loudly
PATH-PRICE-S7.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
PATH-PRICE-S7.outcome: Height and Current lead with "unlimited members." It's a differentiator.

PATH-PRICE-T1.name: One tier
PATH-PRICE-T1.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
PATH-PRICE-T1.outcome: One card, centered, price, 4 to 8 features, one CTA. Reflect ("One plan one price") and Skillshare do this. If price varies by a size variable, put the control inside the card (Kit's subscriber dropdown). Add a small secondary path for big buyers ("Request a demo").

PATH-PRICE-T2.name: Two tiers
PATH-PRICE-T2.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
PATH-PRICE-T2.outcome: Works best when the split is "me vs us" (Personal / Team) or "free vs paid." Highlight the paid one.

PATH-PRICE-T3.name: Three tiers
PATH-PRICE-T3.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
PATH-PRICE-T3.outcome: The default. Name tiers by audience or stage, not Good/Better/Best. Seen: Hobbyist / Creator / Business (Descript), Launch / Grow / Scale (Plain), Starter / Pro / Enterprise (Current).

PATH-PRICE-T4.name: Four tiers
PATH-PRICE-T4.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
PATH-PRICE-T4.outcome: Windsurf, Mistral, Retool, and Firecrawl show four. Only do it when the fourth is a real sales-led tier. Keep card bullets short and put depth in a comparison table. Airtable and Lyssna both use a sticky-header table with grouped sections.

PATH-PRICE-T5.name: Five or more
PATH-PRICE-T5.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
PATH-PRICE-T5.outcome: Only for consumer products with distinct benefit stories. Revolut uses five cards with short descriptions and arrows. Klarna uses tabs plus cards. Never a five-column row of feature bullets.

PATH-PRICE-U1.name: One lockup for price
PATH-PRICE-U1.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U1.outcome: Show price, unit, and billing period together: "$24 per person / month, billed annually." Seen on Descript, Height, Plain. Never split the unit into a footnote.

PATH-PRICE-U10.name: Enterprise says "Custom" in the price slot
PATH-PRICE-U10.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U10.outcome: List what sales unlocks (SSO, audit logs, dedicated support). Don't invent a starting price you won't honor.

PATH-PRICE-U11.name: Define any term that changes the bill
PATH-PRICE-U11.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U11.outcome: Retool footnotes "standard users" vs "end users." If two things look like seats but bill differently, define both below the cards.

PATH-PRICE-U12.name: State tax and currency
PATH-PRICE-U12.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U12.outcome: Mistral says "excluding taxes" and has a currency switch. Do this if you sell across regions.

PATH-PRICE-U13.name: Below the cards, in this order:
PATH-PRICE-U13.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U13.outcome: comparison table (3+ tiers), FAQ, reassurance line (cancel anytime, money-back). *Design judgment, not one observed order.*

PATH-PRICE-U14.name: Mobile stacks cards with the recommended tier first
PATH-PRICE-U14.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U14.outcome: *Design judgment.* Users won't scroll past three tall cards to find the one you want them to see.

PATH-PRICE-U2.name: Annual toggle states its savings
PATH-PRICE-U2.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U2.outcome: "Save 25%," "2 months free," "-20%." Put it next to the toggle, not in a tooltip. Every price on the page must change when the toggle flips. Default to annual only if annual is what you want to sell.

PATH-PRICE-U3.name: Show the annual total when annual is on
PATH-PRICE-U3.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U3.outcome: Copy.ai and Kit both show "$36/mo, billed $432/year." Buyers do the math anyway. Do it for them.

PATH-PRICE-U4.name: One highlighted tier, never two
PATH-PRICE-U4.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U4.outcome: Use a border or elevation plus a short badge ("Most popular," "Recommended"). Do not rely on color alone.

PATH-PRICE-U5.name: Only the highlighted tier gets the primary button
PATH-PRICE-U5.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U5.outcome: Others get secondary style. Descript and Plain do this well. Teachable colors one and blacks the others, which is close but inconsistent when the highlight and the button color disagree.

PATH-PRICE-U6.name: CTA matches the friction
PATH-PRICE-U6.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U6.outcome: Free: "Start free." Paid with trial: "Start free trial." Top tier: "Talk to sales." Do not put "Get started" on every card.

PATH-PRICE-U7.name: Use "Everything in X, plus:"
PATH-PRICE-U7.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U7.outcome: on every tier above the first. Dub, Height, Windsurf, Circle all do it. It cuts repeated bullets and shows the ladder.

PATH-PRICE-U8.name: Limits are numbers, not adjectives
PATH-PRICE-U8.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
PATH-PRICE-U8.outcome: "30 transcription hours / month" beats "generous limits." Keep to about 6 to 8 bullets per card. If a card runs longer, the extra goes in the comparison table.

PATH-PRICE-U9.name: "No credit card required" near the free or trial CTA, only when true
PATH-PRICE-U9.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.

PATH-PRICE-X1.name: Never show only a per-unit rate
PATH-PRICE-X1.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X1.outcome: A rate like "1.8 cents per charge" is meaningless without a sample bill. Add an estimator (Stripe, Vercel, Cofounder).

PATH-PRICE-X10.name: Offer a reset on multi-input calculators
PATH-PRICE-X10.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).

PATH-PRICE-X11.name: Predictability is a feature
PATH-PRICE-X11.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X11.outcome: If you don't meter something, show it as $0. Agentcard lists "$0 per issued card" and "$0 per order" under a flat monthly fee. If you have a spending cap or pause, say so.

PATH-PRICE-X12.name: Outcome pricing needs a definition
PATH-PRICE-X12.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X12.outcome: Intercom prices Fin at "$0.99 per outcome." Any outcome-based price must define what counts as one, on the same screen.

PATH-PRICE-X2.name: Ask in the customer's unit
PATH-PRICE-X2.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X2.outcome: Kit asks "How many email subscribers do you have?" Teak asks "Avg. daily active players." Cartesia converts credits to minutes of audio. If your billing unit is abstract (tokens, credits, blocks), translate it. Mailchimp's "blocks of 25,000 emails" is the version to avoid.

PATH-PRICE-X3.name: Slider plus number input
PATH-PRICE-X3.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X3.outcome: Vercel and Grok pair them. The slider is for exploring, the input is for exactness. Label the tick marks.

PATH-PRICE-X4.name: Show the rate table next to the calculator
PATH-PRICE-X4.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X4.outcome: Stripe highlights the active tier under the slider track. Mailchimp shows the full block-rate table. Buyers want to verify your math.

PATH-PRICE-X5.name: Big estimated total, plus an itemized breakdown
PATH-PRICE-X5.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X5.outcome: Cofounder lists token, compute, and database costs above a large total. Vercel does the same and adds a comparison. Always label it "estimated."

PATH-PRICE-X6.name: Default to a realistic value, not zero
PATH-PRICE-X6.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X6.outcome: Cartesia starts at 45 min. Mailchimp's empty state shows $0.00, which tells the buyer nothing. *My read, not tested.*

PATH-PRICE-X7.name: Show included allowance and overage separately
PATH-PRICE-X7.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X7.outcome: Cofounder: "$20 included." Windsurf: "Add-on credits at $10 / 250 credits." Say what happens when they run out.

PATH-PRICE-X8.name: Recommend a plan from the input
PATH-PRICE-X8.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X8.outcome: Cartesia shows a "Recommended plan" card after you pick volume. Kit disables tiers that can't cover your count ("Max subscribers reached").

PATH-PRICE-X9.name: Say what one unit buys
PATH-PRICE-X9.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
PATH-PRICE-X9.outcome: If you sell credits, give an example ("1 credit = about 2 pages scraped"). ClassPass explains credits in its own page and notes rollover. Rollover is worth stating.

PATH-SET-DANGER-ZONE.name: Danger zone
PATH-SET-DANGER-ZONE.condition: A page has account-, workspace-, or team-level destructive actions.
PATH-SET-DANGER-ZONE.outcome: Group them at the bottom under a Danger zone heading. Each row has a label and helper text on the left and a destructive button on the right. Leave and delete are separate rows.

PATH-SET-EMAIL-CHANGE.name: Flow container and steps
PATH-SET-EMAIL-CHANGE.condition: The user chooses to change their email.
PATH-SET-EMAIL-CHANGE.outcome: A full page at its own route, not a dialog. Two steps shown with a Stepper. Step 1 is the new address, plus the current password when the session is not recent. Step 2 is the code. Follow `JOB-NAVIGATION-POSITION` for the Breadcrumb or Back link, and cap the form container at `--width-form-max`. Step 1 buttons are Cancel (returns to settings, address unchanged) and Next. Step 2 buttons are Back (returns to step 1 with the typed address kept) and Verify. Each step validates before the next. No retype-to-confirm field, since the code already proves the address works.

PATH-SET-EMAIL-CHANGE-DONE.name: Success
PATH-SET-EMAIL-CHANGE-DONE.outcome: Return to the settings page, show the new address in the row with the Verified badge, and confirm with a toast. Until then the row keeps showing the old address.

PATH-SET-IDENTITY-FIELD.name: Email in account settings
PATH-SET-IDENTITY-FIELD.condition: Showing a sign-in identifier such as email.
PATH-SET-IDENTITY-FIELD.outcome: Show it read-only with an explicit Edit control and a Verified badge when verified. Edit starts `[PATH-SET-EMAIL-CHANGE]`. Never a plain input with a Save button.

PATH-SET-INTEG-ACTIONS.name: Connect, configure, disconnect
PATH-SET-INTEG-ACTIONS.condition: Choosing row actions for an integration.
PATH-SET-INTEG-ACTIONS.outcome: Not connected: Connect. Connected: Configure when there are settings, plus a quiet Disconnect. Disconnect is never the primary button and is red only if it deletes data. A Connect that leaves the app shows an external-link icon.

PATH-SET-INTEG-GROUPS.name: Connected before available
PATH-SET-INTEG-GROUPS.outcome: Show Connected above Available, each with a count. Rows are a list by default. Use a card grid only when browsing a large catalog, and add search and a category filter there.

PATH-SET-INTEG-LOCKED.name: Plan-gated integrations
PATH-SET-INTEG-LOCKED.condition: An integration needs a higher plan.
PATH-SET-INTEG-LOCKED.outcome: Show it disabled with the plan requirement stated. Do not hide it. This differs from role-denied items, which are hidden.

PATH-SET-MEMBERS-INVITE.name: Adding a member
PATH-SET-MEMBERS-INVITE.outcome: The Invite button opens a Dialog with email and role. Use an inline email field with an Invite button only when inviting is the main job of the page. The toast names the invited address.

PATH-SET-MEMBERS-LIST.name: Member list
PATH-SET-MEMBERS-LIST.condition: Listing members of a workspace or team.
PATH-SET-MEMBERS-LIST.outcome: Columns are member (name and email), role, and status. Row actions follow `[PATH-B-ROW-ACTIONS]`, so Remove and other secondary actions sit in the DropdownMenu. The Invite primary button sits at the top right of the table. Narrow layout follows `[PATH-B-NARROW]`.

PATH-SET-MEMBERS-SELF.name: Current user and owner rows
PATH-SET-MEMBERS-SELF.condition: A member row is the current user or the owner.
PATH-SET-MEMBERS-SELF.outcome: Label the current user's row "You". The owner row has no Remove. The current user's action is Leave, not Remove. Removing someone else uses an AlertDialog and notifies the removed member afterward.

PATH-SET-MEMBERS-STATES.name: Pending and active rows
PATH-SET-MEMBERS-STATES.condition: A member row is pending or active.
PATH-SET-MEMBERS-STATES.outcome: Pending rows get a Pending badge and the menu actions Resend invite and Remove. Active rows get Edit role and Remove. When the role list is short, role can be an inline Select that saves instantly.

PATH-SET-NOTIF-CHANNEL-OFF.name: Channel not connected
PATH-SET-NOTIF-CHANNEL-OFF.condition: A channel column exists but the channel is not connected, for example Slack.
PATH-SET-NOTIF-CHANNEL-OFF.outcome: Keep the column visible and disabled, with a link to connect it.

PATH-SET-NOTIF-DIGEST.name: Digest
PATH-SET-NOTIF-DIGEST.condition: The product sends a digest email.
PATH-SET-NOTIF-DIGEST.outcome: Put its Switch above the matrix as its own row, separate from the per-event preferences.

PATH-SET-NOTIF-MATRIX.name: Events by channel
PATH-SET-NOTIF-MATRIX.condition: There are two or more channels and three or more event types.
PATH-SET-NOTIF-MATRIX.outcome: Events are rows and channels are columns, grouped under category headers. Each cell is a Switch when changes save instantly, or a Checkbox only when the page has an explicit Save. With one channel, use a plain list of Switches. Below the `sm` container width, each event stacks with its channels listed beneath it.

PATH-SET-OTP-DELIVERY.name: Where the code goes
PATH-SET-OTP-DELIVERY.outcome: Send the code to the new address. The current address stays active until the code verifies. The body names the exact address and offers a way back to correct it. State the code length, and state the expiry when the code expires. After a successful change, notify the previous address.

PATH-SET-OTP-ERROR.name: Wrong or expired code
PATH-SET-OTP-ERROR.condition: The code is wrong or has expired.
PATH-SET-OTP-ERROR.outcome: Show the error inline directly under the field with righter's Helper Text, using an icon plus text, and put every cell in the error state. Keep the digits, selected so typing replaces them. Never a toast for this. An expired code also brings the Resend link into focus. Copy and component choice come from righter.

PATH-SET-OTP-RESEND.name: Resend
PATH-SET-OTP-RESEND.condition: The user did not receive the code.
PATH-SET-OTP-RESEND.outcome: A text link under the field. After each send, disable it and show the remaining wait in or beside it. Do not hide it. The wait length is a product setting, not a Vois value. A resend clears the cells, because the old code stops working, and confirms with a toast.

PATH-SET-OTP-SUBMIT.name: Verify button
PATH-SET-OTP-SUBMIT.outcome: A primary Verify button in the step footer, replacing Next, disabled until every cell is filled. Back is the secondary. While verifying, show an inline Spinner in the button. Do not submit automatically on the last digit.

PATH-SET-REMOVE-TYPED.name: Typed confirmation
PATH-SET-REMOVE-TYPED.condition: The deletion is irreversible or high-impact, such as a workspace, team, or account.
PATH-SET-REMOVE-TYPED.outcome: The user types the object's name before the destructive button enables. The body lists what will be lost with counts and states any recovery window. It always uses a full modal, never a bottom sheet. Dialog width follows `[PATH-D-SIZE]`, which is the small tier.

PATH-SET-ROW-LAYOUT.name: Preference rows
PATH-SET-ROW-LAYOUT.condition: Laying out preference rows, each with a label and one control.
PATH-SET-ROW-LAYOUT.outcome: Label and optional helper text (Description style) on the left, control on the right, centered vertically. Group header above the rows. Rows separated by dividers. No container card or shadow around a group. Cap the content column at `--width-form-max` and space groups with `gap-10`. When the container is narrower than the `sm` value (`37.5em`), stack the control under its label.

PATH-SET-SAVE-EXPLICIT.name: Explicit save for text and multi-field blocks
PATH-SET-SAVE-EXPLICIT.condition: A settings block has text inputs or more than one related field.
PATH-SET-SAVE-EXPLICIT.outcome: Save stays disabled until a value has changed and every required value is valid. Cancel restores the last saved values. Both sit in the block, not in a footer.

PATH-SET-SAVE-INSTANT.name: Instant save for single values
PATH-SET-SAVE-INSTANT.condition: The user changes a Switch, Select, or Radio that stands alone on a settings page.
PATH-SET-SAVE-INSTANT.outcome: Persist on change and confirm with a toast. If the save fails, revert the control and surface the failure with whichever component righter's decision tree picks. No Save button.

PATH-SET-VIEW-EDIT-BLOCK.name: Where the view state still applies
PATH-SET-VIEW-EDIT-BLOCK.condition: A settings block holds details that are mostly read and rarely changed, such as legal name, business address, or billing details.
PATH-SET-VIEW-EDIT-BLOCK.outcome: Use the view state by default and enter the edit state on an explicit Edit action, as `settings-pages.md` describes. Preference blocks are always editable and skip the view state.

PATH-TABLE-BULK-BAR.name: Bulk action bar
PATH-TABLE-BULK-BAR.condition: One or more rows are selected.
PATH-TABLE-BULK-BAR.outcome: Show a bar anchored to the table with the selected count, 2 to 3 visible actions with the rest in a DropdownMenu, and a clear-selection control. The destructive action is last and visually distinct. A persistent bar with disabled actions at zero selected is fine when the table is mainly used for bulk work.

PATH-TABLE-BULK-DESTRUCTIVE.name: Bulk destructive actions
PATH-TABLE-BULK-DESTRUCTIVE.condition: A bulk action deletes, archives, or otherwise cannot be undone cheaply.
PATH-TABLE-BULK-DESTRUCTIVE.outcome: Confirm first and state the count. Use an AlertDialog (see JOB-CONFIRM-DESTRUCTIVE). If the action can be undone, skip the dialog and offer undo in the confirmation toast instead.

PATH-TABLE-COLUMNS.name: Column management
PATH-TABLE-COLUMNS.condition: A complex table has more columns than most users need at once.
PATH-TABLE-COLUMNS.outcome: Offer show or hide, reorder, and pin, plus a Reset to default. A column header menu holds per-column actions (sort, move, hide). The first column cannot be hidden.

PATH-TABLE-COMMIT-BATCH.name: Batch save
PATH-TABLE-COMMIT-BATCH.condition: A user edits several cells or rows, or one value's validity depends on another.
PATH-TABLE-COMMIT-BATCH.outcome: Hold edits locally and show an unsaved-changes bar with Save and Discard. Edited cells are visibly marked. Save is blocked while any edit is invalid, with a summary of what to fix. Never drop valid edits because one is invalid. Leaving the page with unsaved edits asks first.

PATH-TABLE-COMMIT-INSTANT.name: Instant save
PATH-TABLE-COMMIT-INSTANT.condition: A user edits one low-risk value in a cell.
PATH-TABLE-COMMIT-INSTANT.outcome: Save on commit (Enter or blur) and confirm with a toast that offers Undo. If the save fails, revert the cell, mark the row, and keep the typed value available to retry. Surface the failure as `PATH-TABLE-ERROR-ROW-ACTION` says.

PATH-TABLE-DENSITY.name: Density toggle
PATH-TABLE-DENSITY.condition: A complex table has a density control.
PATH-TABLE-DENSITY.outcome: Offer Dense, Regular, and Comfortable. Row height and cell padding come from tokens. Simple tables have one density and no toggle. Remember the choice per user.

PATH-TABLE-DRAWER-STEP.name: Step through rows from the drawer
PATH-TABLE-DRAWER-STEP.condition: A user reviews many rows one after another.
PATH-TABLE-DRAWER-STEP.outcome: Put previous and next controls in the drawer, bound to the Up and Down keys. The table row highlight follows. Stepping past the last row on a page loads the next page.

PATH-TABLE-ERROR-BULK-PARTIAL.name: A bulk or import operation partly failed
PATH-TABLE-ERROR-BULK-PARTIAL.condition: Some rows in a bulk action or import succeed and some fail.
PATH-TABLE-ERROR-BULK-PARTIAL.outcome: Show an Inline Alert above the table with the counts. It is contextual to the table, so it is not an Alert Banner. Mark failed rows with an icon or count in the row gutter. Offer a "show only rows with errors" toggle and the choice to continue with the rows that are ready. When users cannot fix rows in place, offer an export of the failed rows. Name the real cause on each failure.

PATH-TABLE-ERROR-CELL.name: A cell or field is invalid
PATH-TABLE-ERROR-CELL.outcome: Show the message next to the field. In a drawer form it sits under the field. For a cell it opens in a tooltip or popover. Validate on commit or blur, not on every keystroke. Tint the cell and add an icon. Keep what the user typed.

PATH-TABLE-ERROR-FOCUS.name: Focus and announcement
PATH-TABLE-ERROR-FOCUS.condition: A commit, save, or load fails.
PATH-TABLE-ERROR-FOCUS.outcome: Move focus to the first error. Announce errors through an aria-live="polite" region. Never clear the user's data to show an error.

PATH-TABLE-ERROR-ROW-ACTION.name: A row action failed
PATH-TABLE-ERROR-ROW-ACTION.condition: A delete, archive, status change, or similar action on one row fails.
PATH-TABLE-ERROR-ROW-ACTION.outcome: If the UI updated optimistically, roll it back. Mark that row with an error state and offer Retry. Surface the failure with whichever component righter's error decision tree picks, anchored to the row where it can be. The row is the anchor for the error, not the page.

PATH-TABLE-EXPAND-ROWS.name: Expandable rows
PATH-TABLE-EXPAND-ROWS.condition: A row has sub-rows or a short secondary detail.
PATH-TABLE-EXPAND-ROWS.outcome: Use a leading chevron button that toggles aria-expanded. Expanded content stays inside the table. If the detail is a full record, use the drawer instead.

PATH-TABLE-FILTER-BUILDER.name: Filter builder on a complex table
PATH-TABLE-FILTER-BUILDER.condition: A complex table has many filterable fields.
PATH-TABLE-FILTER-BUILDER.outcome: Use rows of field, operator, value, with Add filter, Apply, and Clear filters. Keep applied filters visible as chips after the builder closes.

PATH-TABLE-FILTER-SIMPLE.name: Filters on a simple table
PATH-TABLE-FILTER-SIMPLE.condition: A simple table has one or two filter dimensions.
PATH-TABLE-FILTER-SIMPLE.outcome: Use a single Filter control that opens a Popover. Applied filters show as dismissible chips under the toolbar. Search sits on the left of the toolbar and Filter is pinned top right (PATH-PAGE-SORT-FILTER).

PATH-TABLE-INLINE-EDIT.name: Inline cell edit
PATH-TABLE-INLINE-EDIT.condition: A cell is editable in place.
PATH-TABLE-INLINE-EDIT.outcome: A single click or Enter on a focused cell enters edit mode. Esc cancels and restores the value. Enter commits. Show the cell's edit state with a visible border, not just a cursor. If the table is a grid with arrow-key cell navigation, use role="grid". Otherwise keep a plain table.

PATH-TABLE-KEYBOARD.name: Keyboard
PATH-TABLE-KEYBOARD.condition: A table has rows users act on repeatedly.
PATH-TABLE-KEYBOARD.outcome: Up and Down move row focus. Enter opens the row. Space toggles selection. Esc closes the drawer. Cmd or Ctrl plus Enter saves an edit. Show the shortcut hints where a drawer has them.

PATH-TABLE-NARROW-OPEN.name: Row open on a narrow screen
PATH-TABLE-NARROW-OPEN.condition: A row opens its record below the sm container width.
PATH-TABLE-NARROW-OPEN.outcome: The drawer takes the full width and shows a back control instead of a close control. Back and the URL behave as they do on a wide screen. A record with tabs, a timeline, or related records still escalates to a full page.

PATH-TABLE-NARROW-ROW.name: Stacked row anatomy
PATH-TABLE-NARROW-ROW.condition: A table is below the sm container width and stacks its rows (4 or fewer columns, see PATH-B-NARROW).
PATH-TABLE-NARROW-ROW.outcome: The first column is the row title. Show up to three more values under or beside it: one or two secondary values below the title, one trailing value aligned to the end, and status as a Badge. Nothing is dropped. With 4 or fewer columns every value fits. The whole row is the tap target and opens the record.

PATH-TABLE-NARROW-SELECT.name: Selection on a narrow screen
PATH-TABLE-NARROW-SELECT.condition: A narrow list has bulk actions.
PATH-TABLE-NARROW-SELECT.outcome: Selection is a mode. An explicit Select action enters it, and the checkbox column appears only then. The header shows "N selected" with Select all and Cancel. The bulk bar sits at the bottom of the screen with 2 to 4 actions, the destructive one last and in the destructive color. A destructive action confirms with the count before it runs. Leaving the mode clears the selection.

PATH-TABLE-ROW-CLICK.name: Row click target
PATH-TABLE-ROW-CLICK.condition: A row opens a detail view when clicked.
PATH-TABLE-ROW-CLICK.outcome: The first-column value is the real link or button, so keyboard, screen readers, and middle-click work. The row click is an enhancement on top. Clicks on checkboxes, action menus, and links inside the row do not open the drawer.

PATH-TABLE-ROW-STATES.name: Row states
PATH-TABLE-ROW-STATES.outcome: Support these: default, hover, focus-visible, selected, active (its drawer is open), editing, saving, error, just-added, and disabled or archived. Each has a distinct visual that does not rely on color alone.

PATH-TABLE-SAVED-VIEWS.name: Saved views
PATH-TABLE-SAVED-VIEWS.condition: Users repeat the same combination of filters, sort, and columns.
PATH-TABLE-SAVED-VIEWS.outcome: Offer named views as tabs or a view switcher above the toolbar. A view stores filters, sort, columns, and density. Show an unsaved-changes state when the current setup differs from the saved view.

PATH-TABLE-SELECT-ALL-PAGES.name: Select across pages
PATH-TABLE-SELECT-ALL-PAGES.condition: A paginated table has a full page selected and more results exist.
PATH-TABLE-SELECT-ALL-PAGES.outcome: Offer a "select all N" control next to the selection count. Say how many rows an action will touch before the user confirms it.

PATH-TABLE-SELECT-CHECKBOX.name: Checkbox column
PATH-TABLE-SELECT-CHECKBOX.outcome: Add a leading checkbox column. The header checkbox is tri-state (none, some, all on this page). Shift-click selects a range. Selected rows get a tint and a checked box, never tint alone. Simple tables have no checkbox column.

PATH-TABLE-SEMANTICS.name: Table semantics
PATH-TABLE-SEMANTICS.outcome: Use a real table element with th and scope. Do not rebuild it from div elements. The sortable header is a button inside the th.

PATH-TABLE-SORT.name: Sorting
PATH-TABLE-SORT.outcome: Clicking its header cycles ascending, descending, none. The sorted header shows direction and carries aria-sort. One active sort unless the product genuinely needs more. Sort resets paging to page 1.

PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-FILTERED.name: Empty, filtered
PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-FILTERED.condition: Search or filters removed every row.
PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-FILTERED.outcome: Say that filters caused it and offer Clear filters. Use an inline message, not a full EmptyState.

PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-FIRST.name: Empty, first use
PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-FIRST.condition: The user has never created anything here and can create from this screen.
PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-FIRST.outcome: Show an EmptyState with the primary create action. Headers stay visible.

PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-NATURE.name: Empty by nature
PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-NATURE.condition: No rows is a normal, good state, such as no live calls or no open issues.
PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-NATURE.outcome: Say so plainly. No call to action.

PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-PERMISSION.name: Empty by permission
PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-PERMISSION.condition: The user cannot see any rows because of their role.
PATH-TABLE-STATE-EMPTY-PERMISSION.outcome: Say that access is the reason and who can grant it. Do not show the first-use create action.

PATH-TABLE-STATE-LOAD-ERROR.name: Table failed to load
PATH-TABLE-STATE-LOAD-ERROR.outcome: Replace the rows with an inline panel in the table area: the cause when known and a Retry. Toolbar and headers stay, so filters survive. Not a full-screen modal.

PATH-TABLE-STATE-LOADING.name: Initial load
PATH-TABLE-STATE-LOADING.condition: A table is loading for the first time.
PATH-TABLE-STATE-LOADING.outcome: Show the real column headers and skeleton rows that match the loaded column widths. Never a full-area spinner.

PATH-TABLE-STATE-REFETCH.name: Refetch
PATH-TABLE-STATE-REFETCH.condition: A filter, sort, or page change reloads data.
PATH-TABLE-STATE-REFETCH.outcome: Keep the stale rows on screen with a small busy indicator. Do not blank the table.

PATH-TABLE-STATE-TRUNCATED.name: Results limited by plan
PATH-TABLE-STATE-TRUNCATED.condition: A plan limit hides some rows.
PATH-TABLE-STATE-TRUNCATED.outcome: Put a notice above the table that says so, with the upgrade action. Do not leave it to the footer.

PATH-TABLE-URL-STATE.name: State lives in the URL
PATH-TABLE-URL-STATE.condition: A table has search, filters, sort, page, or an open row.
PATH-TABLE-URL-STATE.outcome: Keep each of them in the URL. Reload, back, and a shared link restore the same view, including the open drawer.

FIELD-CHECK-BLUR.title: Check on blur
FIELD-CHECK-BLUR.rule: The default time to check a value is when the user leaves the field, then again on submit. Once a field shows an error, re-check on every keystroke so the error clears the moment it is fixed.

FIELD-FORMAT-BLUR.title: Format on blur and keep the cursor
FIELD-FORMAT-BLUR.rule: Apply grouping and separators when the user leaves the field. If you format while typing, keep the caret where the user left it, including after a paste in the middle of the value. A format that jumps the caret to the end is a bug.

FIELD-FORMAT-NOT-PROOF.title: A format check is not proof
FIELD-FORMAT-NOT-PROOF.rule: A value that has the right shape may still be wrong: a well formed email may bounce, a valid VIN may belong to another vehicle. Word the check as what it did ('This does not look like a VIN') and use an explicit action (send a code, decode the VIN, confirm the address) when you need proof.

FIELD-INCOMPLETE.title: Incomplete is not invalid
FIELD-INCOMPLETE.rule: A value that is not finished yet has no error. A VIN with 14 of 17 characters is incomplete, not wrong. Show a counter or a hint, never an error, until the user leaves the field or submits.
never: red error text while the user is still typing

FIELD-PASTE.title: Never block paste or autofill
FIELD-PASTE.rule: Let the user paste into every field and let the browser and password manager fill it. Do not cancel the paste event, do not split a value across boxes that reject a pasted whole, and do not set autocomplete off on a field the browser can fill (email, phone, postal code, name, one-time code). Clean the pasted value afterwards: trim it, strip separators.
never: one box per digit that rejects a pasted code

FIELD-PREFILL-CONFLICT.title: Show both when sources disagree
FIELD-PREFILL-CONFLICT.rule: When two sources give different values, show both with their sources and ask the user to choose. Never pick one silently.

FIELD-PREFILL-FIX.title: Let the user fix a prefilled value
FIELD-PREFILL-FIX.rule: A prefilled value is an ordinary editable value. Never lock it. Editing it changes its source to 'entered by you'.

FIELD-PREFILL-NOTME.title: 'Not me' clears it
FIELD-PREFILL-NOTME.rule: When the prefilled value may belong to someone else (a shared device, a lookup that matched the wrong record), offer a clear action ('Not me' or 'Clear') that removes the value and the source label together.

FIELD-PREFILL-SOURCE.title: Show the source of a prefilled value
FIELD-PREFILL-SOURCE.rule: When a value was filled in for the user, show it in the field and show where it came from (their profile, the last policy, a lookup, an imported document). Use a small source label next to the field, not a tooltip only. A prefilled value looks different from one the user typed.

FIELD-PREFILL-SUGGEST.title: Low-confidence guesses are suggestions
FIELD-PREFILL-SUGGEST.rule: Fill the field only when you are confident. A weaker guess appears as a suggestion the user accepts with one action, not as a value already in the box.

FIELD-PREFILL-UNDO.title: Undo an accepted prefill
FIELD-PREFILL-UNDO.rule: After the user accepts a suggestion or a bulk prefill, keep an Undo available until they leave the page or submit.

FIELD-SENSITIVE-LOOKUP.title: No lookup per keystroke
FIELD-SENSITIVE-LOOKUP.rule: Never send a sensitive value to a server as the user types. Send it once, on an explicit action or on submit.
never: type-ahead on an SSN or license number

FIELD-SENSITIVE-MASK.title: Mask after entry, with a reveal
FIELD-SENSITIVE-MASK.rule: Show a sensitive value masked once the user leaves the field, keeping the last four characters, with a control to reveal it. Keep paste and password managers working. Do not mask a value the user is still typing.

FIELD-SENSITIVE-STORAGE.title: Sensitive data stays out of URLs, logs, analytics and error reports
FIELD-SENSITIVE-STORAGE.rule: SSN, driver's license number, one-time codes and other sensitive fields never go in a URL or query string, a log line, an analytics event, or an error report. Strip them before any of those are written. Personal fields (name, email, phone, address, date of birth) stay out of URLs and analytics events.
never: a sensitive value in a query string
a sensitive value in console.log or an error tracker payload
a sensitive value as an analytics event property

FIELD-SENSITIVE-SUGGEST.title: No suggestions on sensitive fields
FIELD-SENSITIVE-SUGGEST.rule: Turn off autocomplete history and suggestion lists on sensitive fields (autocomplete off), and never show earlier values in a dropdown.

FIELD-TEXT-CODES.title: IDs and codes are text
FIELD-TEXT-CODES.rule: A value you do not do arithmetic on is a string: postal code, VIN, license number, SSN, phone, one-time code, policy and claim numbers. Use type text with the right inputmode, never type number, which drops leading zeros, adds spinner arrows, and changes the value on scroll.
never: type=number for a code, ID or phone

FIELD-TIMING-ACTION.title: When to check: on an explicit action
FIELD-TIMING-ACTION.rule: For anything that costs money, sends a message or needs proof: Verify a code, Look up a VIN, Check availability. Do not run these on blur.

FIELD-TIMING-BLUR.title: When to check: on blur
FIELD-TIMING-BLUR.rule: The default for format checks. Run it when focus leaves the field.

FIELD-TIMING-PAUSE.title: When to check: after a pause
FIELD-TIMING-PAUSE.rule: For a lookup the user is waiting on (availability, type-ahead). Wait 300 to 500 ms after the last keystroke. Drop any answer that arrives for an older value.

FIELD-TIMING-SUBMIT.title: When to check: on submit
FIELD-TIMING-SUBMIT.rule: For checks that need more than one field, and for required fields left empty. Never show a required error on a field the user has not reached yet.

FIELD-TIMING-TYPING.title: When to check: while typing
FIELD-TIMING-TYPING.rule: Only for help, never for errors: a character counter, a strength hint, a count of what is left. Never block a keystroke, never show an error.

FIELD-TYPEAHEAD-DEFAULTS.title: Type-ahead defaults
FIELD-TYPEAHEAD-DEFAULTS.rule: Start searching after 300 to 500 ms of pause and 2 to 3 characters. Show 3 to 6 results. Drop any response that arrives for an older query. Never pick the first result for the user automatically: the user chooses. Keep the record's ID apart from its label, and store the ID.
never: auto-selecting the first result on Enter or blur
storing the label as the value

FIELD-VALUE-SPLIT.title: Keep the shown value and the stored value apart
FIELD-VALUE-SPLIT.rule: The text in the box is for people, the stored value is for the system. Format what is shown (grouping, hyphens, a currency separator). Store one canonical form (E.164 for a phone, digits for an SSN, cents for money). Never read the shown text back as the stored value.
